screening_results.reason: The study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making), with event-related contrasts for decision and outcome events (e.g., Inflate, Success, Win) and parametric modulation by explosion probability, satisfying within-task contrasts related to risk. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted (with spatial normalization, smoothing, and cluster-level correction via Monte Carlo/FWE thresholds) and results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing decisions involving risk (probabilities) and effort (multi-attribute value-based choices). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (non-parametric permutation-based inference with TFCE and FWE correction) and reported with significant clusters and MNI coordinates (tables/figures). Contrasts/regressors relevant to risky decision-making and decision difficulty were tested (SV parametric modulator, H/entropy, and NRNE>NRME), yielding whole-brain results. Thus it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI of risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/SV/choice difficulty), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), and I7 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-alternative olfactory pleasantness decision task (decision taken during second odor). The authors report within-task contrasts and regression analyses related to decision difficulty/discriminability (ΔI; analogous to hard>easy or correlations with task easiness) and correct vs error contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group random-effects level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 analyses with reported peak coordinates and statistical values (small-volume corrections reported), satisfying the reporting requirements. Therefore the study meets I4 (task fMRI in humans), I5 (within-task contrasts / regressors related to perceptual/decision difficulty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (coordinates and results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (the CUPS task) performed during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts (risky vs. non-risky trials and parametric modulators for risk and reward) and behavioral correlations, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected results, tables of coordinates and figures), meeting I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: the study is not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results and is an empirical whole-brain task activation study. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (emotional voice discrimination; biased vs. unbiased decisions). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., unbiased > biased on affective voices, biased > unbiased) and contrasts involving affective versus neutral voices. Group-level voxelwise GLM analyses were performed and thresholded (p<0.05 FDR) and the authors state that ROI masks were applied to whole-brain results (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps exist and were used to derive ROI findings). Results are reported as peak activations and connectivity contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, empirical data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants using the Cambridge Gambling Task, which is a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk and outcome processing (e.g., win > lose; majority vs rest; parametric analysis of unexpected wins), uses group-level random-effects GLM and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with FDR correction and cluster thresholds (coordinates/tables and figures provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (7T) performing a task that manipulates ambiguity, uncertainty, and expectation while making decisions about sequence correctness. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to ambiguous decision-making (e.g., ambiguous > unambiguous; ambiguous > incongruent; A21 > A12) and order contrasts (2-1 > 1-2). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM12, second-level random-effects, FWE cluster correction) and coordinates/results are reported. Thus it satisfies I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing four perceptual decision-making tasks (face–house, happy–angry, audiovisual synchrony/asynchrony, RDM). The paper reports within-task contrasts that map difficulty (e.g., noisy/hard > clear/easy; low coherence > high coherence) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (second-level one-sample t-tests) with FWE correction and tables of coordinates. Thus it meets all perceptual-DM inclusion criteria (I4, I5) and the whole-brain reporting requirements (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (parametric modulation by pump number; contrasts such as pumps after cash-out vs after explosion), with thresholding and coordinates provided in tables/figures. The Methods, Results, and Discussion are present in the provided full text. Thus all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that collected BOLD data while participants performed a risky decision-making task (choice between risky gambles and certain outcomes) (I4). The analyses report within-task contrasts distinguishing gamble versus certainty choices using searchlight MVPA (split-half correlations producing a distance metric d comparing gamble vs certainty) during pre- and post-stimulus periods (I5). Analyses were conducted across the whole brain with Talairach standardization and group-level one-sample t-tests with cluster-threshold correction, producing voxelwise statistical maps and reported cluster coordinates and tables (I6, I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain task activation maps and a contrast comparing uncertain reward anticipation to a no-incentive condition (satisfying I5, I6, I7), it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task in the sense required by the review. The slot-machine paradigm was passive (no decisions or choices that influence outcomes), so it fails I4 (task is not a decision-making task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded because I4 is not satisfied.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a sequential risk-taking task (risky decision-making), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts derived from the risky task (e.g., Opt vs Nopt, Nopt vs Devil, GF vs MF), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected results and MNI coordinates (conjunction and contrast maps, FWE-corrected clusters), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses and includes unmasked whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants using a probabilistic monetary decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-reward/risk > low-reward/risk; monetary > control). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxelwise t-maps, tables of coordinates, figures). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., Fin vs Nin, Hin vs Nin, In vs Out, Fin+Hin > Nin), conducted group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with reported activation maps and cluster-level FWE-corrected results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans who performed a decision-making task involving probabilistic treatment risks and benefits (participants imagined having MS and chose whether to take medications with varying side-effect probabilities and efficacies). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (mild > severe and severe > mild) and associated behavioral, SCR, activation, and PPI results. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise GLM (SPM12) with FWE correction and results presented in tables/figures. Thus it meets I4 (task-based fMRI of risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risk contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, includes whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulated decision uncertainty both as probabilistic (externally attributed frequency; Exp.1) and knowledge-based (internally attributed ambiguity; Exp.2). It reports within-task contrasts (uncertain > control), parametric contrasts of increasing uncertainty, and between-experiment comparisons. Imaging used whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses with voxelwise maps reported as Z-scores and peak coordinates (tables/figures). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (task fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making), I5 (relevant within- and between-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that implements a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination) during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making and signal strength (e.g., FaceSignalStrength > HouseSignalStrength, parametric modulation by difficulty/signal strength, FaceDecision > HouseDecision, hard/ easy manipulations), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (initial z-threshold, cluster correction) and whole-brain results are reported (nucleus accumbens, vmPFC, hippocampus, etc.), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

The study used fMRI (MID task) to examine reward anticipation and receipt, reporting voxelwise, whole-brain task effects and correlations with early life stress. However, the in-scanner task is a reward-processing/anticipation paradigm, not a risky-, ambiguous-, or perceptual-decision-making task; no within-scanner contrasts reflecting risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or hard > easy are reported. Thus it fails the critical inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Whole-brain reporting and coordinate/figure descriptions are present (satisfying I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used a risky gambling (Goal-Instructed Gambling) task during scanning and reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses and contrasts. The paper presents within-task contrasts related to risk/quota (e.g., quota severity: Easy<Low<High<Imp) and gPPI contrasts (Low/High > Non/Imp etc.), reports activation clusters and coordinates, and describes preprocessing and group analyses (SPM8) with correction for multiple comparisons. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual categorization task (array-averaging of color/shape) while scanned. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with parametric contrasts relating BOLD to task difficulty/uncertainty (mean-related and variance-related uncertainty), provide peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results, and include figures/tables describing whole-brain findings. Thus it meets the review’s focus on perceptual decision-making and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of human adolescents performing the Iowa Gambling Task (an ambiguous decision-making task), reporting within-task contrasts (advantageous vs. disadvantageous choices; wins vs. losses) and computational modeling. The paper presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (in addition to ROI analyses), reports whole-brain clusters (e.g., PCC, MPFC) with cluster-level thresholds, and describes results in text and figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study reporting group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses with contrasts comparing easy vs. difficult decisions (e.g., easy > difficult) and provides coordinate tables—so it meets I5 (relevant within-task contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported with coordinates). However, the tasks are value-based affective decisions about pleasantness (olfactory and thermal stimuli) and choices about whether to repeat a stimulus, rather than risky, ambiguous, or clearly perceptual decision-making tasks as required by the review. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI but the scan was performed during a working-memory (n-back) task, not while participants performed a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task (the Iowa Gambling Task was administered behaviorally outside the scanner). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making) and I5 (a task contrast directly related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). Although the paper reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses (WM 2-back > 0-back) and regressions linking those activations to IGT performance, the target whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are for a WM task, not a decision-making task, so I6 (whole-brain task map for decision-making) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5, I6. Exclusion IDs met: none. Result: EXCLUDED.

This fMRI study used the weather prediction task (probabilistic classification) and includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses reported in tables/figures. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). However, the paper does not report a within-task or between-task contrast that maps onto risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts required by I5 (e.g., high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, risk > safe, hard > easy). The reported neuroimaging contrasts are primarily group differences (control > stroke) and task effects are focused on presentation vs feedback and group contrasts; no explicit ambiguity/risk-related contrast (e.g., low vs high predictive value) with corresponding whole-brain maps relevant to the meta-analysis is presented. Therefore it fails to meet I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full-text reports an fMRI experiment (experiment 3) during a gamble task involving risky decisions under uncertainty (meets I4). The analysis includes within-task contrasts that compare gamble vs sure choices and an interaction contrast indexing choices related to risk/bias (meets I5). Imaging was analyzed at the group (second-level one-sample t-test) voxelwise using SPM and reports task-evoked statistical maps; although a priori amygdala masking was used, whole-brain group results (e.g., ventral striatum) are reported/explored (meets I6 and I7). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans using an fMRI-adapted Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), which is an ambiguous decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (decision-making > control) and group-level activation maps, with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (p<0.05, cluster thresholding) and group comparisons (controls vs T2DM). Results are reported in text/figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, or resting-state analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (stacks accumulating bricks), satisfying the review topic. It includes within-task contrasts (200 ms vs baseline, 400 ms vs baseline) and regression analyses linking BOLD to behavioral measures of urgency. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses were performed and reported (third-level analyses, conjunction analysis, cluster-corrected maps with peak MNI coordinates). Results are presented with coordinates and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral paradigm, fMRI acquisition and whole-brain analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing probabilistic/uncertain decision-making tasks (balls-in-a-bottle and personality survey), directly addressing ambiguous decision making. The primary contrast compares decision making under uncertainty versus certainty (uncertainty > certainty), satisfying an ambiguity-related within-task contrast. Analyses are voxelwise, group-level whole-brain SPM results (fixed-effects across 8 subjects) reported with corrected voxelwise statistics and stereotaxic coordinates and figures. Thus the paper provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported as coordinates/figures. Limitations (small N and fixed-effects models) do not violate inclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures, so fulltext appears complete.

This fMRI study uses a probabilistic reversal learning task (human participants performing a decision-making task) and reports within-task contrasts (PFB vs NFB-Stay/NFB-Switch), so inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are met. However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (extraction of mean activity from ACC, VS, vmPFC masks) and the primary comparisons are ROI-level; there are no reported group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables for an unmasked whole-brain task effect. Although the authors mention comparing to standard SPM analyses, results are presented for ROIs and discretised state analyses. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet I6. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that includes a prospective risk mixed-gambles task and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. It reports within-task contrasts related to prospective risk (parametric modulation by winning probability/risk level) and subjective-value/predicted-acceptance maps, with whole-brain correction and provision of unthresholded statistical maps on NeuroVault. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results clearly reported and shared). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Full text shows an fMRI study in healthy humans performing a risky decision-making task (I4 met). Group-level whole-brain GLM analyses were conducted (FEAT/FLAME) and whole-brain contrasts are reported in the text/figures (I6 and I7 met). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrast that directly indexes risky decision-making (e.g., "risky > safe", "high-risk > low-risk", or similar) — instead the reported voxelwise contrasts concern conditioned stimulus (CS) cue processing (Touched_CS > Shocked_CS) linked to a model-derived valuation parameter; decision-period regressors were modeled as regressors of no interest and no explicit risky>safe decision contrast is provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, and the study should be excluded. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in 24 healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task). The paper reports within-task contrasts (anticipation vs experience; gain vs loss vs draw; deck A–D comparisons) relevant to risky/ambiguous decision-making. Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise with family-wise error correction and coordinate reporting, and brain activation maps/tables are described. The full text includes Background, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (delayed match-to-category with auditory and tactile sweeps). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level searchlight MVPA with voxelwise t tests and TFCE multiple-comparison correction, reporting corrected statistical parameter maps (figures/tables) that reflect task-related effects (cross-decoding of category, modality, and direction). Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/decoding related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study used task-based fMRI in human adolescents performing the Wheel of Fortune risky decision-making task (I4). It reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk (25%) > low-risk (75%); 25/75 risk/reward > control) (I5). The manuscript explicitly states that whole-brain group-level analyses were conducted and reports peak voxel coordinates in tables (I6, I7). Although many reported results are ROI-based with small-volume correction, whole-brain analyses were performed and task-evoked activation peaks are provided, satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

The article reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making gambling task (choice between control and experimental gambles), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (experimental vs control, high vs low probability, high vs low gain/loss), satisfying I5. The analysis reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps using FLAME and OLS with cluster correction and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains whole-brain task activation maps, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination) while in the scanner. It reports within-task contrasts (Report > Follow and Follow > Report) and parametric modulators of confidence (confidence-related activity), which are task-evoked contrasts linked to perceptual decision-making/metacognitive reporting. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM8 with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates reported in tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study reports original fMRI data collected while healthy human subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task (face vs car categorization with manipulated phase coherence), satisfying I4. The analysis includes task-related contrasts/conditions tied to perceptual difficulty/coherence (perithreshold/low coherence vs high coherence; hard > easy type manipulations) and EEG-informed regressors modulated by coherence and task, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported (mixed-effects group analysis, cluster-corrected z-maps, coordinate/figure reporting), satisfying I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that acquired whole-brain EPI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under probabilistic uncertainty). The authors report task-related, model-derived reward prediction error (RPE) parametric modulator contrasts and compare these effects between OCD patients and controls. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-extent FWE-corrected results with MNI coordinates and table/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are described in the main text with coordinates and statistics; supplementary main-effect maps are also referenced. The task involves probabilistic reward contingencies (80/20) and reversals, which constitutes decision-making under uncertainty/risk; the RPE contrast is directly relevant to decision-making processes. Therefore I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (gender classification of morphed faces) in healthy human participants and reports within-task comparisons between ambiguous and unambiguous stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (functional MRI during a perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (within-task comparison related to perceptual ambiguity). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (variance of BOLD within preselected bilateral SPL and IPL masks) and statistical comparisons limited to these ROIs; no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates/whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map). Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E3 (ROI-only analyses / no whole-brain voxelwise group map).

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm), includes within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of pump number; mean pump vs control-balloon), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses with coordinates and figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This longitudinal study acquired task-based fMRI while participants performed the Risky Gains Task (a risky decision-making paradigm) and reports within-task contrasts (risky vs safe decisions; risky wins vs risky losses). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level (AFNI LME and voxelwise thresholding with cluster correction), with coordinates and figures/tables of significant clusters reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of imaging methods and results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain task activation reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (tactile grating orientation) with concurrent fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM, SPM) and thresholded SPM maps (voxel p≤.001, cluster p≤.05 FWE) and contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (GOT task > motor control; easy vs difficult; parametric modulation by confidence; post-decision confidence regressors). Whole-brain results are reported and mapped, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study examines perceptual decision-making in MRI vs behavioral sessions and includes actual MRI sessions (Experiments 1–2) and manipulations relevant to perceptual difficulty (coherence: hard > easy). Therefore I4 and I5 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures of fMRI activations; it focuses on behavioral results and response-time (LBA) modeling. The manuscript explicitly states that the fMRI sessions for some experiments were previously published, but this article itself does not provide whole-brain task activation maps or coordinates required for meta-analysis. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and provides no qualifying whole-brain results. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria from the provided list exactly apply (no ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting), so exclusion is based on failure to meet I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (attend, speed/accuracy, confidence). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., stimulus/perceptual judgment > rest; task > background) tied to perceptual decision processes (selection, criterion setting, evaluation). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported and thresholded (with FWE cluster correction) and unthresholded maps are available. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group–only, and it is an empirical report with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. I4: Healthy human participants underwent fMRI while performing a well-validated risky decision-making task (the Balloon Analog Risk Task). I5: The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., prepump/risky > pre-cash out/safe; univariate contrast maps and reported contrasts such as “risky > safe”). I6: Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (univariate contrast maps across subjects, whole-brain classifier and searchlight analyses). I7: Whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables (searchlight maps, tables of regions, univariate contrast maps) and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=13) performing a navigation task that explicitly manipulates partial observability/uncertainty (ambiguity) and examines neural correlates of uncertainty resolution. The paper reports within-task contrasts (goal-search > visuomotor control) and model-based regression analyses tied to HCP entropy (uncertainty), which correspond to ambiguous decision-making contrasts (e.g., ambiguous task > control) and parametrically relate to uncertainty. Imaging analyses were performed at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and reported thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans where adolescents performed a lottery-based risky decision-making task during BOLD scanning. The authors report a within-task parametric contrast indexing risk (coefficient of variation of chosen gambles; high-risk > low-risk) and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (cluster-level FWE correction). Results (text, figure, and table) report task-evoked whole-brain activation (including a right amygdala cluster) related to risk. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making tasks (criterion comparison and signal detection) with task manipulations of uncertainty/difficulty. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (parametric uncertainty regressors) and searchlight MVPA, with cluster-corrected statistical maps and Talairach coordinates referenced (figures/tables). Contrasts relate directly to perceptual decision-making uncertainty (e.g., difficult vs. easy/parametric uncertainty). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task that includes parametric modulation by a state-change uncertainty (SCU) regressor, i.e., an uncertainty-related contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected maps) and ROI analyses. The SCU regressor provides an uncertainty contrast akin to 'high uncertainty > low uncertainty', satisfying the ambiguous decision-making contrast requirement. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete.

This empirical fMRI study used a risky decision-making task (child-friendly Cake Gambling Task) with human participants and reported within-task contrasts directly related to risk (High-Risk > Low-Risk) and outcome (Gain > No-Gain). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (voxelwise t-tests, ANOVAs, thresholding, and MNI coordinates provided; supplementary tables referenced). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and task effects are reported rather than only between-group interactions). Therefore it satisfies I4–I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (delayed match-to-category of auditory and tactile sweep direction). The paper reports within-task contrasts and classification of up vs. down sweeps, and presents group-level, whole-brain analyses (univariate GLM group t-maps and surface-based multivariate searchlight results) with cluster-based correction and conjunction across modalities. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study acquired fMRI in healthy adult humans performing an explicit probabilistic learning task that requires ongoing probability estimation under uncertainty (ambiguous decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts examining uncertainty/confidence (e.g., high vs low confidence), surprise (unexpected vs expected), and estimation update, which map onto ambiguity/uncertainty-related contrasts (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (GLMs, cluster-corrected maps, tables of peak coordinates and supplemental figures), and results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that used a sequential risk-taking task during scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/outcome evaluation (e.g., Optimum > Miss, Miss > Devil; Mood and Context contrasts tied to risk decisions), satisfying I5. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (SPM8 random-effects flexible factorial; cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates reported), meeting I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment of methods and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination) with task-evoked fMRI during decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts (face > house) and trial-wise analyses linking BOLD to behavior, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, maps, and reported Talairach coordinates/tables). Results are reported in figures/tables and interpreted in intro/methods/results/discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults (N=18 analyzed) who performed risky decision-making tasks (lotteries) and social/strategic decision-making tasks (stag-hunt and entry games) during fMRI. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing uncertain (B) vs sure (A) choices and contrasts across task types (e.g., entry > lotteries/stag-hunt), and they performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster FWE correction and report peak MNI coordinates. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and coordinates. Thus the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic object reversal task (pORT) involving reward-based decision-making with known probabilistic contingencies (80%), satisfying the review’s decision-making domain (risky/probabilistic). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., ‘learned’ vs ‘not yet learned’, parametric modulation across learning bins) tied to the decision-making and feedback phases, meeting I5. Group-level mixed-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted in SPM2 to identify voxels in the ventral striatum (statistical threshold P<0.001 uncorrected) and coordinates are reported (x=12,y=16,z=-5), indicating whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results and satisfying I6 and I7. Although subsequent analyses focus on an ROI defined from the group contrast, the ROI was derived from a group-level whole-brain contrast rather than being ROI-only, so E3 does not apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore all required inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (audiovisual synchrony/asynchrony judgments). It includes within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., asynchrony > unisensory, synchrony > unisensory, and comparisons between asynchrony and synchrony), and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses with coordinates and figures. Although the paper also performs DCM effective connectivity analyses, whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported and thresholded at the group level. The full-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced) is present. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a task that manipulates rule uncertainty (certain vs uncertain), directly addressing ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports within-task contrasts (uncertain > certain and certain > uncertain) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (Z-statistic images thresholded and cluster-corrected), with figures/tables describing the whole-brain results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (tactile spatial pattern discrimination) that manipulates task difficulty (intact, partially scrambled, fully scrambled) and reports decision-related contrasts. The authors performed group-level random-effects whole-brain GLM analyses with parametric modulators (RT/difficulty), conjunction analyses, cluster correction (Monte Carlo), and report Talairach coordinates and activation maps (figures and supplementary table). They also report MVPA results. Thus the study satisfies: I4 (human fMRI during a perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulation related to difficulty e.g., hard>easy), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I7 (results reported via maps and coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed a perceptual decision-making task (near-threshold Gabor detection) with concurrent confidence judgments, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to perceptual decision-making and expectation effects (e.g., expectation-incongruent > expectation-congruent; unexpected > expected), satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM contrasts with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates and tables, satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (E3), are not solely connectivity/resting-state (E4) and include task activation maps rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an uncertain/ambiguous decision-making task (matching-pennies), with explicit contrasts related to uncertainty/feedback (e.g., feedback > no-feedback; uncertain > certain) and attentional load. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects, voxelwise group analyses (P < 0.001) and lists ROIs from that whole-brain analysis; results are presented across experiments, including event-related and block designs. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies I4 (human fMRI during ambiguous/uncertain decision-making), I5 (task contrasts related to uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants who performed a risky decision-making task (Cups Task) during scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (risky vs nonrisky choices; gain vs loss; choice×condition interactions) and correlation contrasts with anxiety scores (meets I5). Analyses were conducted at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain statistics (FSL FLAME1) with cluster-based correction and reported whole-brain results in the text/tables/figures (meets I6 and I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Includes human fMRI data collected while participants performed a temporally-extended probabilistic categorization task (perceptual/categorical decision-making). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts related to decision evidence, confidence and urgency, and presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) SPM analyses with multiple-comparison corrected maps and coordinate tables. Thus it satisfies I4 (task+fMRI), I5 (within-task contrasts tied to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), and I7 (results clearly described and reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI maps of task-evoked prediction-error responses (satisfying I6) and reporting is acceptable per I7, it does not provide contrasts that map onto risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required by I4–I5. The task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning paradigm emphasizing prediction-error signals and gain vs. loss motivational context; contrasts focus on PE and gain>loss (and group interactions), not on risk vs safe, ambiguity vs non-ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty contrasts. Therefore I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual categorization task (random-dot motion), meeting I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (parametric effects of motion coherence, split parametric contrasts, accuracy-related parametric maps and interaction contrasts), meeting I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM maps with cluster-size correction and reported tables/figures of significant regions, meeting I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (interactive risky-choice game) and reports task-related contrasts (anticipation to punishment: non-match vs. match; reward outcome contrasts), satisfying I4 and I5. However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the risky task contrast; regional task effects were assessed via ROI templates (amygdala and NAcc) and group comparisons reported as ROI-based t-tests. The manuscript mainly reports seed-based whole-brain functional connectivity and DTI voxelwise results, but lacks an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map or coordinates for the task contrasts. Therefore I6 is not satisfied. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (task results reported as ROI analyses without whole-brain task results) and E4 (seed-based connectivity reported without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is an original human fMRI study that acquired task-evoked, whole-brain BOLD data while participants performed a perceptual decision-making (sparse vs. dense categorization) task with an uncertainty/opt-out response. The paper reports multiple within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., uncertainty > correct, correct > uncertainty), parametric distance-to-bound (difficulty) modulators (hard vs. easy effects), and near/far (near-to-bound vs far-from-bound) contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs (FSL/FLAME1) with cluster correction; results are presented as whole-brain maps and tables of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures, tables, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (58 adolescent girls) who performed a probabilistic risky decision-making task (modified Jackpot) during MRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Play > Pass, Gain > Loss, Low-risk > High-risk) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and supplementary tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task with risk/uncertainty and ambiguity (choices between gains/losses with learnable sequence). The paper reports within-task contrasts (gains vs losses; correct vs wrong; ambiguous vs unambiguous feedback; exploratory vs proficiency phases) relevant to risky/ambiguous decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects SPM2 results with MNI coordinates and tables provided. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and coordinates).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between high-risk and low-risk gambles). The authors report within-task contrasts of interest (high-risk > low-risk) and present group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps/thresholds and peak coordinates (tables and figures). Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky sequential decision-making task (I4). The analysis includes within-task contrasts/regressors directly related to risk and outcome statistics (expected value, variance/risk, skewness) and tests parametric effects of risk-related variables (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM with random-effects group statistics and results reported with stereotactic coordinates and voxelwise thresholds (I6), and whole-brain results/coordinates are reported in the text and figures (I7). The full-text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral and fMRI), Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with parametric manipulation of sensory evidence (suprathreshold vs perithreshold). The authors report within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., suprathreshold > perithreshold, hard > easy analogs) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with statistical maps, coordinates, and thresholds. Results are reported in figures/tables and the methods describe standard whole-brain GLM procedures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for perceptual-DM studies are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. It used functional MRI in human adolescents performing the HiLo decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (I4). The primary contrast of interest compares the pure uncertainty (50%) condition to the other probabilistic conditions (high uncertainty > lower uncertainty), which is directly relevant to ambiguous decision-making contrasts (I5). Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise methods (FLAME) with corrected cluster thresholds and report whole-brain results in figures and tables (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (E3), not exclusively connectivity/resting-state analyses (E4), and not limited to between-group contrasts without accompanying whole-brain task effects (E5). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=13) who performed a sequential reaction-time perceptual choice task (SRTT) during scanning. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts relating neural activity to information-theoretic measures (e.g., mutual information—effectively high vs low predictability), which constitute task-related contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making. Analyses were conducted as group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses and significant clusters and peak coordinates are reported (tables and figures). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6 and I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a 4-arm bandit decision-making task probing uncertainty/exploration (decision-making under risk/ambiguity). It includes within-task contrasts and regressors directly related to uncertainty/decision-making (explore > exploit, entropy regressors, reward omission effects, pupil–BOLD regressions). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with cluster-based permutation correction and whole-brain statistical maps (uploaded to NeuroVault). Therefore it satisfies I4 (human fMRI on decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results presented as whole-brain maps/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical with original fMRI data). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (risky vs. safe; risky/safe vs. chance) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster thresholds, peak coordinates, and tables/figures describing the activation maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, group analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain contrasts), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a well-defined risky decision-making task (modified cups task) during scanning (meets I4). It reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risk processing (e.g., risky > sure; self vs. other; target×situation interactions) (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level models with results reported using whole-brain FWE correction and peak coordinates (meets I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between risky and safe monetary lotteries) with task-evoked, group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses (parametric probability regressor) and reported whole-brain results (tables/figures/text). Contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (risky > safe; modulation by probability) are explicitly reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (delayed matching-to-sample with identical images to induce uncertainty and checking). It reports within-task contrasts related to decision-making under uncertainty (DFCB+ vs DFCB−) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, ANOVA, whole-brain regression) with results described in text and figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in humans using the Risky Gains Task (risky decision-making) with group-level statistical analyses. It includes within-task contrasts related to risk (risky versus safe) and reports voxel-wise analyses; the manuscript states whole-brain patterns of activation and group differences are provided in supplemental figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging, preprocessing, voxel-wise LME), Results (behavioral and imaging), and Discussion. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (risky > safe contrasts / group by decision interactions), I6 (group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain results referenced in supplements), and I7 (results described and presented in main text and supplements). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (core sections present).

This is an empirical human fMRI study of a perceptual decision-making (time-pressured READ-M/Go/No-Go) task. It reports within-task contrasts (behaviorally correct vs. incorrect; Correct Go vs. Correct No-Go; Incorrect No-Go etc.) and uses whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (GLM, searchlight AUC and p-value maps, group-level registration and permutation testing). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplementary tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/seed-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that measured brain activation while subjects performed risky and intertemporal decision-making tasks (meets I4). The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts directly relevant to risk and delay (e.g., Risk > Control, Risk > Delay, Delay > Risk, and choice-predictive contrasts) (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects comparisons using FSL/FLAME with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-correction; results are reported as statistical maps and coordinate tables (meets I6 and I7). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence). The paper reports within-task contrasts relating task difficulty/coherence (e.g., inverse parametric effect: low coherence > high coherence), correct vs incorrect contrasts, and trialwise RT correlations. Whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses and group-level statistical maps (fixed-effects group summary) are reported and coordinates are provided in tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, group-level fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a decision-making task under outcome uncertainty (jar-draw task), satisfying the review topic. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making (e.g., information-gathering > counting; decision event > counting; uncertainty acceptance/avoidance conjunctions). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM5 results with FWE thresholds and coordinate tables/figures provided. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a sequential predictive-inference task that requires decision-making under uncertainty. The authors report within-task analyses tied to computational measures of uncertainty (relative uncertainty, change-point probability) and behaviorally relevant contrasts (learning rates, policy), and they map these effects using whole-brain searchlight RSA and group-level voxelwise statistics (t-maps, cluster-based permutation testing) reported in figures and tables. Thus it satisfies: I4 (fMRI during decision task under uncertainty/ambiguity), I5 (within-task contrasts/analyses related to uncertainty/risk-relevant variables), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that investigated decision making under risk and ambiguity using an Ellsberg-style urn task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (parametric modulators for belief updating, value updating, and expectancy violation), provides activation maps and cluster-level inference, and tables/figures of results. Task contrasts and parametric effects directly relate to ambiguous and risky decision-making. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reward-guided decision-making task involving exploration–exploitation and contingency reversals. The paper reports a within-task contrast of exploratory > exploitative trials (analogous to high uncertainty > low uncertainty / ambiguous > non-ambiguous) and model-based prediction-error contrasts, with group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps (whole-brain FWE-corrected task effects across participants are reported). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (at least one relevant contrast: exploratory>exploitative), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without whole-brain task effect, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical fMRI study administered the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) to human adolescents while acquiring BOLD data. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., risky > safe choices; anticipation; wins > losses) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses (ANCOVA, within-group maps, cluster results) with ROI follow-ups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, fMRI acquisition, whole-brain analysis), Results (whole-brain and ROI results), and Discussion, so core article content is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making), I5 (relevant within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results described and reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s domain-specific inclusion criteria. Specifically, I4 and I5 are NOT met: the task is a probabilistic reward-learning / reversal-learning paradigm focused on reward prediction errors (valence and surprise) rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task, and the reported contrasts pertain to RPE valence and surprise rather than contrasts of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguity > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). The study does meet I6 and I7: it reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI analyses and provides whole-brain results (tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a decision-making task that manipulated risk and ambiguity (Card-Deck paradigm). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (decision under risk vs. decision under ambiguity; bet vs. safe; bet under risk vs. bet under ambiguity). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise GLM results reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction, with activations presented in tables and figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria for risky/ambiguous fMRI studies are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles) during scanning with a within-subject threat manipulation, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/value coding (e.g., ESV safe vs threat, task-related activations, threat>safe contrasts) and trial-wise value regressors tied to choices, satisfying I5. The authors ran group-level, voxelwise analyses and report whole-brain exploratory results (FWE-corrected activations for pain-related contrasts) and provide MNI coordinates for value-related effects; results are described in text with coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., risky vs nonrisk, parametric linear risk contrast, explosions vs cashouts) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL mixed-effects, cluster-corrected maps, tables/figures). Reporting includes whole-brain results and ROI supplementary analyses. The full article contains introduction, methods (task, imaging, analysis), results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (Stoplight) during scanning, with within-task contrasts (e.g., Go > Stop, Stop > Go, Crash > NoCrash) directly related to risk. Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with tables of coordinates, cluster thresholds, and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and GLM), Results (voxelwise group analyses), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (GO/NO-GO shape-identification), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) and reported task-evoked contrasts/parametric effects (predictive information modulation) with clusterwise FWE correction and coordinates. The manuscript reports whole-brain activation maps, ROI and connectivity follow-ups, and fits the meta-analysis scope of perceptual decision-making. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level task data while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (categorizing clear vs noisy emotional faces). They report within-task contrasts including noisy > clear (hard > easy analogue) and faces > rest, and present voxelwise second-level maps and coordinate tables (FDR-corrected). The manuscript contains full Methods, Results, and Discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing accept/reject decisions involving monetary gains and losses (cost–benefit choices with uncertain outcomes), which qualifies as decision-making under risk/uncertainty. The study reports within-task contrasts relevant to decision difficulty (hard > easy) and model-driven contrasts tied to decision variables, meeting the requirement for a task-related contrast. Analyses are whole-brain group-level voxelwise GLMs with corrected cluster-level inference and tables of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a multi-step gambling task that manipulates risk (quota severity) during scanning and reports task-evoked activation maps and contrasts related to risky decision-making (quota severity and strategy-optimization contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (two-sample and one-sample t-tests with cluster correction) and activation clusters are described, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The paper also reports PPI connectivity but not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an intertemporal decision-making task that manipulates time-ambiguity. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly testing ambiguity (Ambiguous > Exact and related SV Amb vs SV Ex contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE cluster-corrected results, conjunction analyses, and supplementary materials). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs. house discrimination) with manipulations of difficulty and response mode. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., hard > easy, DR > RT) and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with peak coordinates reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (task fMRI in humans), I5 (perceptual decision contrasts such as hard>easy), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Recommended inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a gambling decision-making task manipulating uncertainty (Win vs. Lose blocks), directly addressing ambiguous/risky decision-making. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Lose vs. Win; Task Condition effects) and group-level whole-brain GLM activation analyses (SPM8) with results presented as group activation maps and tables of coordinates. Although the paper also includes ROI-to-ROI connectivity analyses, it clearly reports unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps used to define ROIs. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of ambiguous/risky decision-making and provides whole-brain group-level results suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling/guessing task that manipulates uncertainty/risk (predicting colour vs suit). The paper reports task contrasts directly related to decision-making under uncertainty (predicting/guessing > reporting; suit > colour; interactions), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported activation tables and figures. Therefore it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making tasks (four separate perceptual paradigms). It includes within-task contrasts that index perceptual difficulty (e.g., noisy > clear, low coherence > high coherence, asynchrony > synchrony / multisensory > unisensory), and explicitly reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with random-effects models and FWE-corrected cluster results (Table 1 and text). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (satisfying I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper presents whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only), is not exclusively connectivity/resting-state, and includes within-task contrasts rather than only between-group comparisons. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met.

Only the abstract is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract the study reports an fMRI paradigm during a decision-making task, so I4 (fMRI during risky/decision task) appears satisfied. However, the abstract does not provide sufficient detail to confirm that at least one task-related contrast relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making is reported (I5) nor that group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps or coordinate-based whole-brain results are presented (I6/I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because the full text is unavailable, I cannot verify critical inclusion criteria (I5 and I6) required for the meta-analysis, so the study is excluded pending full-text review.
