This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a sequential virtual foraging task involving probabilistic foraging vs certain waiting (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts (e.g., probability of foraging success, optimal-policy value differences, choice uncertainties, discrepancies) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests with whole-brain FWE correction and MNI coordinates reported). Thus it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI in humans on a risky decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/decision variables), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I7 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=15) using a decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (ambiguous vs. unambiguous landing stimuli) and risk via financial incentives. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making (e.g., High vs. Low uncertainty; Financial_High vs. Neutral_High) and correlations with behavioral indices (d'). Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain SPM8 GLMs; results are reported as statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables with thresholding and SVC procedures. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for (I4) task-based human fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making, (I5) relevant within-task contrasts, (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and (I7) reporting of results in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion; supplementary material not required for inclusion.

This is a simultaneous EEG-fMRI empirical study (healthy adult humans) in which subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion direction discrimination) during fMRI acquisition. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results: parametric contrasts linking BOLD to behavioral confidence ratings and to an EEG-derived single-trial confidence regressor, with cluster-corrected maps and MNI coordinates (Supplementary Tables and figures). Thus the study includes (I4) fMRI during a perceptual decision task, (I5) within-task/task-related contrasts (parametric modulation by confidence and EEG-derived confidence), (I6) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps, and (I7) coordinates/figures clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (Mean Color > Mean White; Linear Color > Linear White) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected) with tables/figures of results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (whole-brain main effects and group comparisons), and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (random dot motion) task with a matched control. The authors report voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise ANOVA, cluster correction via AFNI 3dClustSim) and present tables/figures of significant clusters, including contrasts of the perceptual task (dots) > control task (arrows) and interactions identifying ramping activity. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision task), I5 (perceptual task > control contrast and related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study collected fMRI in healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (ambiguous vs control) and reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguity/risk prediction errors, so inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are satisfied. However, the paper uses predefined ROI analyses (12 ROIs per hemisphere) and reports mixed-model ROI statistics without presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures. Thus it does not meet I6 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (the cups task) during whole-brain fMRI acquisition and analysis. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., risky > safe, win > loss) and parametric modulations (experienced risk, experienced reward), and performs group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses with whole-brain correction. Results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans that manipulated objective vs. subjective uncertainty during a decision-making task (deck selection) — i.e., an ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., certain vs. uncertain sequences; first-draw and accumulating evidence contrasts) and group- and within-group whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results with cluster-level correction and tables of MNI coordinates. Thus it meets criteria for (I4) task-based fMRI during ambiguous decision-making, (I5) within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/ambiguity, (I6) whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation maps, and (I7) reporting of coordinates/tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effects, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (dot motion/color coherence), satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts relating difficulty/coherence (e.g., low vs high coherence; linear parametric contrasts for attended/ignored coherence), meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported (fixed-effects group summary maps, whole-brain parametric contrasts shown in figures and summarized in Table 1), fulfilling I6 and I7 (results presented in figures/tables described in text). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task that manipulates risk (probability) and delay (time) concurrently. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., task vs. summation control) and a parametric regressor (PTT) related to subjective value/risk-time trade-off; results are reported with voxelwise FWE-corrected maps and uncorrected maps and referenced tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4–I7 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in which human adolescents performed a well-established risky decision-making task (Stoplight Task) while scanned, and presents within-task contrasts (e.g., Stop vs Go, risky outcomes) comparing maternal vs non-maternal adult presence. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported (whole-brain t-tests, cluster correction) with tables/figures of results. Thus it satisfies I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and are empirical whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a four-armed bandit decision-making task with probabilistic monetary rewards (exploration/exploitation), satisfying the review scope. The paper reports within-task contrasts and model-based regressors related to decision-making (novel vs familiar choices; prediction-error and novelty-bonus components tied to choice and outcome), meeting the requirement for at least one decision-related contrast. Analyses were conducted at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain random-effects SPM5 analyses (maps and activations reported, with coordinates and small-volume correction for predicted regions), fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Experimental Procedures; supplemental material not required. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study (N=14) had human participants perform a four-armed bandit decision-making task under uncertainty (exploration vs exploitation), providing a within-task contrast classifying trials as exploratory (high uncertainty) versus exploitative. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 analyses with whole-brain corrected activations and coordinates (e.g., frontopolar cortex, intraparietal sulcus), and present voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates in the text and supplementary material. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task type (uncertainty/ambiguity), within-task contrast related to uncertainty/exploration, whole-brain group-level analyses, and acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of risky decision making that reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results and contrasts between decision types. The methods specify whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster thresholding z>2.3, whole-brain corrected p<0.05) and report contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., P_max > G_max/L_min; magnitude-sensitive compensatory choices > simplifying choices). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the risky-gains task (risky decision-making) with a within-task contrast of risky (40,80) versus safe (20) choices. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (cluster-corrected voxelwise maps and extracted cluster statistics/figures), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and whole-brain GLT/LME analyses), Results, and Discussion. The study is empirical task-evoked fMRI (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans where adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts for risky vs safe decisions (go vs stop) and peer vs parent contrasts, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and multiple-comparison corrected, with results available on NeuroVault, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study used an ROI-focused fMRI analysis (a priori ROI masks with small-volume correction) and does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are met (Iowa Gambling Task fMRI; reported risky vs. safe and wins vs. losses contrasts). Inclusion criteria I6 is NOT met (no whole-brain task-evoked, voxelwise group maps reported). I7 is also not met because the reported coordinates/activations stem from ROI analyses rather than whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that acquired task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning (decision-making under uncertainty/risk) task, and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked analyses (one-sample and independent-samples t tests) with familywise-error whole-brain correction and SVC when applicable. The manuscript includes within-task contrasts related to feedback/risk (punished vs rewarded; learning-rate, prediction-error, expected-value parametric modulators) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, satisfying the meta-analysis objectives. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that directly investigates risky decision-making. It includes within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., Play > Pass, Gain > Loss, and the Context × Decision interaction reflecting risk preference shifts). Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM8 with whole-brain voxelwise statistics (pFWE cluster-corrected) and reported peak coordinates and clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain results. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging, GLM), Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using a mixed-gambles risky decision-making task performed in the scanner (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk decisions (Accepted Trials > Baseline, Rejected Trials > Baseline, Accepted > Rejected, Rejected > Accepted) and group comparisons (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (cluster thresholding reported) with peak coordinates reported (I6,I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include unmasked whole-brain task effects. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic two-armed bandit task (decision-making under uncertainty/probabilistic reward), with task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests, FWE-corrected maps) and reported task-related contrasts/parametric modulators (e.g., chosen value Q at choice; RPE/R-Q at outcome) with peak coordinates. Thus it provides whole-brain task activation maps related to decision-making under uncertainty and reports coordinates. Meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This article includes an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (cued discrimination of degraded fearful and neutral faces). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (paired t-tests and mixed-model ANOVA) with whole-brain results and MNI coordinates, and presents voxelwise maps and corrected statistical results linking cue- and stimulus-related activity to behavioral measures. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task/stimulus contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (reporting of whole-brain results with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a gambling (risky decision-making) task, reporting within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., Risk vs Norisk; decisions after Norisk vs Riskwin; Risk > Norisk) and showing group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (and small-volume corrections reported for hypothesized regions). Full article provides introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that administered a decision-making task under uncertainty (HiLo game; ambiguous decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguity/uncertainty (linear uncertainty contrast excluding 50% condition; direct 50% vs 100% comparisons; incorrect>correct feedback contrasts). Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects procedures (FLAME) with cluster correction and reported cluster coordinates (e.g., ACC x=-2,y=22,z=38), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Caveat: small sample size and task simplicity noted in limitations but do not preclude inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used task-based fMRI during perceptual (RDM) and rule-based decision-making with a decision–redecision paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME) and task > control contrasts as well as regressions with difficulty/uncertainty (e.g., task trials vs control trials during redecision; uncertainty-level regressions; difficulty manipulations), satisfying perceptual decision-making contrasts (perceptual task > control, low coherence/hard trials). Whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding procedures are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated sensory evidence (high vs low coherence). It includes within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty (Low>High and High>Low sensory evidence) and motor-preparation contrasts, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME1+2) with cluster correction; results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (motion direction discrimination), satisfying I4. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts based on coherence (low vs high coherence/parametric modulation), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests with permutation and cluster-level FWE correction) are reported and thresholded across the whole brain, satisfying I6. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinates, satisfying I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked whole-brain maps; not only resting-state/connectivity analyses; empirical data in healthy adults).

This is a whole-brain, group-level fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly manipulates referential uncertainty and risk in pronoun resolution and reports contrasts directly indexing ambiguity/uncertainty and risk (e.g., Undetermined > Directly Determined, Indirectly Determined > Directly Determined) as well as a parametric analysis of uncertainty. Methods describe whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 analyses and random-effects group results (FDR-corrected and uncorrected thresholds) reported in tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making with appropriate contrasts and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that used a risky decision-making task (modified BART) during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., parametric Active Pumpsparametric vs Control Pumpsparametric; cash-out and explosion contrasts; RW vs TSD comparisons), satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM results (voxelwise thresholding, cluster correction) with tables/figures of activations, satisfying I6 and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity, and includes whole-brain task effects).

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing decision-making tasks (delay discounting and probability discounting). The probability discounting (PD) task involves risky decisions (probabilistic vs certain rewards) and includes within-task contrasts (probability option vs fixed option) relevant to risky decision-making. The authors performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and report group activation differences (tables/figures/coordinates). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI while healthy human participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task involving explicit high uncertainty trials, which maps onto ambiguous decision-making. It reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to decision-making (shift>stay for choice under uncertainty; reward>punishment for outcome processing). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (FLAME) with TFCE family-wise error correction and whole-brain results are reported in the text/figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only without unmasked task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified beads probabilistic decision-making task (ambiguity) with human participants (patients and controls). Reported contrasts include task vs control (lake reasoning > color naming) and critical event-related contrast (last fish [decision] > all previous fish) directly indexing ambiguous decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are presented with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of peak coordinates. ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are provided. The paper therefore meets I4 (task-based fMRI of ambiguous decision-making), I5 (relevant within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing risky decision-making tasks (choices between risky and safe options). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk > low-risk, risky > safe) and provides group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain correction and peak coordinates. Results and methods include random-effects group analyses and report whole-brain and small-volume corrected activations; coordinates and figures are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants (bipolar patients and healthy controls) that used a risky decision-making task (modified Roulette) during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/probability (e.g., high- vs low-probability gains, gains vs losses) and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (reported in text, figures, and Supplementary Tables; whole-brain thresholds and FWE-corrected results are described). Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts without task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary materials are referenced but not required.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (card-guessing/betting) task. The manuscript reports multiple within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., betting-related contrasts: self- vs. computer-selected, previous win vs. loss, and their interactions), and presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with activation tables and figures (thresholds, cluster sizes) and one-sample t-tests at the group level. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. Thus it meets I4 (task fMRI in humans), I5 (within-task risky-DM contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study in humans performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task, with scans acquired during task performance. The authors report within-task contrasts (experimental/risk block > control block) and group-level comparisons (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) and provide voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (thresholds and cluster correction described) as well as tables/figures of results. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures; ROI analyses are present but not exclusive. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a reward-guided probabilistic reversal learning task with uncertain (probabilistic) outcomes, which corresponds to decision-making under uncertainty/risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reward vs. punishment; prediction error regressors, positive vs. negative PE) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM, FWE-corrected results, coordinates/tables provided). Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI task-based study of decision-making with whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=32) performing a predictive-inference/spatial-prediction task involving uncertainty and belief updating (perceptual/decision-making under uncertainty). The authors report within-task contrasts for model-derived uncertainty/surprise variables (CPP, RU) and reward value and perform group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected permutation testing). Results include whole-brain maps, conjunctions, and contrasts relevant to perceptual/uncertainty-related decision-making. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results clearly described in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (N=15) using a monetary decision-making task that parametrically manipulates reward probability and uncertainty (risky/uncertain decisions). The paper reports within-task contrasts modeling reward uncertainty (e.g., high vs low uncertainty), reward magnitude, expected value, and prediction error, and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM5 with thresholded statistical maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a financial risky decision-making task while scanned. The paper reports within-task contrasts and analyses related to risk and valuation (e.g., MESSAGE vs NO MESSAGE, ignoring vs following advice, correlations with weighted lottery value/probability weighting), uses group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-reported), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical).

The study is excluded because its fMRI task (delay discounting task) measures intertemporal decision-making rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps were reported using FLAME with cluster coordinates) and I7 (whole-brain results are reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no contrast matching risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study acquired group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation while healthy human participants performed a probabilistic reinforcement learning task in which choices had differing reward probabilities (decision-making under uncertainty/risk). It reports within-task contrasts related to decision/outcome processing (e.g., positive>negative feedback, negative>positive feedback; feedback type × cycle-phase interactions) and behavioral correlations with performance, which index decision-making under probabilistic risk. The manuscript describes whole-brain, group-level analyses (thresholds and tables reported), with whole-brain results and ROI SVCs; findings are presented in tables and figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during human decision-making task under probabilistic risk), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision outcomes), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (moving dots), meeting I4. It also compares coherence levels (e.g., 50% vs 12%), meeting I5. However, the paper reports ROI-based directed connectivity (spectral Granger causality) among predefined nodes and net causal outflows; there is no presentation of group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation maps or unmasked whole-brain contrasts in the full text provided. Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6). Exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (only effective/connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Hence EXCLUDED because I4 and I5 met, but I6 not met; exclusion criteria E3 and E4 are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly examines perceptual decision-making under uncertainty (random dot motion task) while scanning. It includes within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual/uncertainty decision-making (e.g., easy vs hard/ambiguous, parametric conformity/dissent, reputation × difficulty interactions) and analyses of anticipatory threat related to joint-performance-based shock probability (risk/anticipation). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t tests, FDR-corrected whole-brain results and tables of coordinates; SVC used for specific hypotheses), satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reports, or non-empirical paper).

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic inference about latent causes (OFC representation of posterior distributions). Although it uses fMRI in human participants and reports whole-brain searchlight RSA results, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required. Specifically, it does not report within-task or between-task contrasts of the form used in risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). Analyses focus on multivariate representational similarity and ROI/searchlight model fits rather than task-evoked voxelwise contrasts directly tied to risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision difficulty. Therefore it fails to meet the review's inclusion criteria. Exclusion rationale summary: exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (task type: not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no relevant contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise contrasts relevant to meta-analysis). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion E3 met: the fMRI analyses were constrained to predefined ROIs and results were reported using small-volume correction (SVC) rather than an unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 - study used task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning decision-making task (uncertainty/ambiguity context); I5 - within-task contrasts (feedback conditions: win, lose-stay, lose-shift and feedback-related contrasts/interactions) were reported. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 - no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported (analyses limited to ROIs with SVC). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it reports only ROI-focused task results without corresponding whole-brain task activation maps (E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making task (Modified Cups Task). It reports within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., decisions after riskloss vs riskwin, riskloss–riskwin) and feedback-related contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (cluster-corrected thresholds, coordinates, figures), and results are reported in text, figures, and coordinates. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans that administered a risky decision-making task (BART) during scanning (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to choice and outcome (choose win–inflate; outcome inflate–explode) relevant to risk/reward processing (I5). The authors conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (stated explicitly; although no significant clusters survived correction, the whole-brain analyses were performed) satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Results and contrasts are described in the text and ROI findings are presented; reporting of whole-brain analyses and contrasts in the text meets I7. The full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a social probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making task (emotion-recognition JTC paradigm), meeting I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguous decision-making (e.g., final decision: last face > previous faces; block contrasts of increasing happiness vs fear), meeting I5. The authors conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and report whole-brain results (p<0.05 FWE-corrected) with tables/figures and ROI follow-ups, meeting I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (E3 not met), no connectivity-only or resting-state-only analyses (E4 not met), and group-level task effects are reported rather than only between-group contrasts (E5 not met). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in human adolescents using the Decision-Reward Uncertainty Task, which manipulates risky and uncertain decision-making. It includes within-task contrasts directly related to risky decision-making (e.g., behavioral risk > reward risk/no-risk) and outcome contrasts (reward > no-reward after risky decisions). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (FLAME), thresholded and reported with cluster coordinates and tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of task, contrasts, and whole-brain results. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for risky/ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study used an fMRI probabilistic feedback expectancy task examining reward anticipation and outcomes, not an active risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses are reported, with voxelwise results and cluster tables) and I7 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is reward expectancy/motivation with instructed motor responses rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task where participants choose between options under risk/ambiguity), and I5 (no within-task contrast reflecting risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, or analogous decision-making contrasts; reported contrasts are gain vs loss anticipation/outcome rather than risk- vs safe-choice contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed a categorization task containing ambiguous trials (inverse base rate effect). The paper reports within-task contrasts/regressors related to ambiguity/uncertainty (trial-by-trial similarity- and dissimilarity-based evidence; analyses of ambiguous > non-ambiguous patterns via MVPA and parametric univariate maps) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (model-based univariate results with cluster correction). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; raw and processed data/maps are publicly available. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (task fMRI in humans on ambiguous decision-making), I5 (task-related contrasts/regressors tied to ambiguity/uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI in healthy adults).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making (mixed-gamble) task with concurrent fMRI. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/expected value (e.g., positive EV > negative EV, neutral EV contrasts, EV × urgency interactions) and uncertainty contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (SPM8 second-level flexible factorial, voxel-level p<0.001 with cluster correction) with whole-brain results reported alongside ROI analyses. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study that collected task-evoked BOLD data while human participants performed a decision-making under uncertainty task (a modified "beads" task). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (DECISION > COUNTING) and group-level voxelwise second-level analyses using SPM5, with activation maps, cluster results and peak coordinates referenced in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, and second-level analyses), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during ambiguous decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast related to ambiguity), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study (22 healthy human participants) in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (predicting occluded trajectory endpoints) while scanned. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts tied to perceptual uncertainty/precision (dynamic-model precision, statistical-model precision, KL divergence, accuracy)—these are task-evoked decision-related contrasts analogous to perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (e.g., low vs high precision). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and reported (thresholded Z-maps, cluster-corrected maps, activation tables and figures). Therefore it meets I4 (human fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical data present). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (piano vs chair categorization with three discriminability levels). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (random effects) with FWE correction, and present parametric contrasts tied to stimulus quality (analogous to hard > easy / low coherence > high coherence) and to response-time variation within fixed stimulus-quality levels. Results are reported as tables of coordinates and figures. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (31 physicians) performing diagnostic decision-making tasks manipulating diagnosticity (uncertainty). The study reports within-task contrasts related to diagnostic uncertainty/diagnosticity (e.g., foreperiod vs high/low diagnosticity first stimulus, epoch contrasts reflecting decision vs vocalization), satisfying contrasts related to ambiguity/uncertainty. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM12 results with FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates reported (conjunction and contrasts), and results are presented in text/figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI meta-analysis of ambiguous/risky/perceptual decision-making (uncertainty domain).

This is an event-related fMRI study in adults performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task). I4 met: fMRI was acquired while participants performed the IGT. I5 met: within-task contrasts were modeled and reported (win minus neutral, loss minus neutral, response phase; contrasts relate to feedback/risk). I6 met: group-level, whole-brain random-effect (voxelwise) analyses were performed (second-level independent t-tests); results reported with voxelwise thresholds and peak MNI coordinates. I7 met: whole-brain results and peak coordinates are reported in the text and figures. Although small-volume correction was applied to a priori OFC regions, whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts without task maps, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that administered a risk-taking/risky decision-making task during scanning and reports within-task contrasts (risk-disadvantageous vs risk-advantageous) and group-level comparisons. The authors performed voxelwise, whole-brain GLM analyses with second-level group analyses, cluster-level FWE correction and report peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes (Table 1, figures). Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures meets acceptable reporting. The study therefore satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (relevant within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (coordinates/figures reported). None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without task effect, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed a decision-making task with probabilistic/uncertain outcomes (learning guesses with 83%, 67%, and 50% reward probabilities). The authors modelled and reported parametric contrasts directly related to uncertainty and prediction errors (e.g., cue-related uncertainty; action-independent and action-dependent PEs), which map onto ambiguous decision-making contrasts (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (SPM8; whole-brain thresholding and cluster correction), and results are reported in the text, figures, and supplementary tables. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a restless multi-armed bandit decision task that manipulates risk, estimation uncertainty, and unexpected uncertainty. The paper presents within-task parametric contrasts (e.g., risk, estimation uncertainty, unexpected uncertainty, learning rate, expected value) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical results (FWE-corrected thresholds, cluster thresholds, and ROI-corrected LC analysis), with results described in text, figures, and supplemental materials. The provided full text includes introduction, methods (imaging and analysis), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports event-related fMRI in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (I4 satisfied). It performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates/tables (I6 and I7 satisfied). However, it does not present any within-task or between-task contrast that directly indexes risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as specified (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The reported contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses, probabilistic errors vs correct responses, preceding reversal errors vs correct responses, and ROI contrasts) index reversal learning and error-processing rather than explicit risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty manipulations; therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 not met; inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7; inclusion criteria not met: I5; exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game). It reports within-task contrasts (Decision Trial − Directed Trial; risky vs sham-directed), and conducts group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise permutation-based analyses (SnPM) with tables/figures of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical limitations).

This study reports an empirical fMRI experiment in healthy adults using a perceptual decision-making task (backward-masking majority function task), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (main effects and interaction contrasts) linking task difficulty/information rate to activation (e.g., AIC, ACC). Whole-brain SPM group analyses with cluster-level correction and voxelwise regression (coordinates and statistics reported) are provided. These meet I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making/information-rate/hard>easy analog), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results clearly reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., risky > safe; punished vs non-punished) and dose effects. It includes group-level whole-brain analyses (with cluster-thresholding) reported in tables/figures as well as ROI analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults using the Wheel of Fortune task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to risk/probability (e.g., risky > safe; low- vs high-probability) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables and cluster thresholds. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, whole-brain results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (I4 satisfied) and it reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (evidence vs. noise; reward bias vs. neutral) (I5 satisfied). However, the paper presents results primarily from ROI-based analyses (time-course extraction from individually defined ROIs and group ANOVAs) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or tables of whole-brain coordinates for the decision contrasts. There are localizer-based maps to define ROIs, but the main decision-related results are ROI analyses only. Therefore it fails to meet I6 (whole-brain evidence) and falls under exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (and thus I7 not satisfied). Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains). It reports task-related contrasts (risky > safe; reward > punishment) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (within-group one-sample t-tests and between-group ANOVAs/t-tests) with coordinates, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task effects, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (accept/reject monetary gambles). The paper reports within-task contrasts and interactions related to risk and safe choices (e.g., accept > reject, risk × accumulated reward, DV × choice) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with clusterwise FDR correction and permutation (SnPM) confirmation, plus coordinates in tables/text. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not include any fMRI data or analyses. It reports behavioral probabilistic reinforcement learning in adults with ASD but no MRI scanning or task-evoked imaging contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no functional MRI scan during the decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task fMRI contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I7 (not applicable because no fMRI results). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 strictly apply (paper is empirical but contains no fMRI data). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that includes a probability-discounting (risky) decision-making task and intertemporal decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts/parametric effects related to subjective value during probability discounting (e.g., brain activity correlating with subjective value in PD, comparisons of PD vs DD), and it uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects second-level analyses) with reported coordinates, thresholding, and supplemental tables/figures. Results are not ROI-only and are task-evoked. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (supplemental material referenced but not required). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded due to E3: the study reports primarily ROI-based analyses and model fits of BOLD responses (averaging time series from retinotopically defined visual areas) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the paper contains stimulus condition contrasts such as different coherence/contrast levels, e.g., low vs high coherence). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants performed an independent fixation/luminance task and passively viewed motion stimuli — they did not perform a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), and I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that directly manipulated risk and ambiguity during a decision-making task (lottery with visible vs occluded bowls), satisfying I4. The paper reports task contrasts comparing ambiguity versus risk (main effects and group-by-condition interaction), satisfying I5. Analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE correction across the whole brain and reported tables/figures of clusters), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for core criteria, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (E3), not solely connectivity/resting-state (E4), and include whole-brain task effects beyond between-group contrasts (E5). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky and ambiguous decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a delayed-match-to-sample recognition task that manipulates sample–probe similarity (match, similar non-match, dissimilar non-match) and memory load. The sample–probe similarity manipulation constitutes a perceptual decision-making difficulty manipulation, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (main effect of sample–probe similarity and pairwise comparisons). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 analyses with FDR correction and coordinates/tables provided. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI reversal learning task and analyses of prediction-error (PE) signals (parametric PE regressors) and their relationships with fluid IQ and stressful life events. While it includes group-level, voxelwise GLM analyses and reports whole-brain results/coordinates (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not test or report contrasts specifically targeting risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The task is a reinforcement learning/reversal paradigm rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation, and no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty are presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (N=15) performing an economic decision-making task that manipulated reward probability and delay (risky/uncertain decisions). The authors report within-task contrasts and parametric regression analyses linking Shannon entropy (uncertainty) to BOLD activity, plus a DM > C2 contrast. Analyses were performed at the group level using random-effects whole-brain voxelwise GLMs and report cluster coordinates and maps. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision task), I5 (within-task/parametric contrasts related to uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/clusters in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a financial risky decision-making task (BIAS). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risky versus riskless choices and gain versus loss outcomes and uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (with global family-wise error correction and small-volume corrections) to localize activation. It therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for task type (risky decision-making), relevant contrasts, and whole-brain group-level results. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (lottery choices) during scanning, meeting I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts/parametric modulators directly related to risk (ΔU, ΔMin, ΔEV; Self vs Other comparisons), meeting I5. The manuscript describes group-level whole-brain GLM analyses and states whole-brain activations are summarized in a table of coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7 (coordinate tables are acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore include for the meta-analysis.

The study meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making: participants performed assurance and chicken games in-scanner) and I5 (within-task contrasts such as AG − CG and AN − NE are reported). However, the paper reports that the exploratory whole-brain analysis produced no FWE-corrected significant voxels and the authors present only region-of-interest (ROI) results (nucleus accumbens, amygdala). They do not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or substantive whole-brain coordinates/thresholded results to include in a whole-brain meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain task-evoked map) and I7 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures) are not satisfied. This violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Excluded on basis of E3.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) decision-making task that involves probabilistic/ambiguous outcomes and behavioral adjustments (relevant to ambiguous decision-making). The authors provide within-task contrasts focusing on lose-shift (negative feedback leading to behavioral change) and other feedback conditions, and conduct group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain results reported, cluster coordinates and figures provided). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making: lose-shift vs other conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain activations; not connectivity-only; empirical task-based fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision making), includes within-task parametric contrasts (modulation of activation by pump number / risk), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, cluster-corrected) with results described in text, figures, and tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and GLM), Results (whole-brain results and permutation testing), and Discussion, so the full article appears complete. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults).

This fMRI study used a probabilistic category learning (weather prediction) task and reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with tables/figures. Thus it provides a task>control contrast (weather prediction > perceptual-motor control) and whole-brain results. However, the meta-analysis objective is fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making. The experimental paradigm here is a non-declarative probabilistic category-learning task rather than a risky, ambiguity-manipulation, or perceptual-difficulty decision-making task as defined for the review. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (task is risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of instrumental probabilistic reinforcement learning (reward and punishment) with contrasts focused on receipt of reward vs no-outcome, punishment vs no-outcome, and prediction errors. While the paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps (meets I6) and provides results in text/tables (meets I7), it does not test or report contrasts specifically related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., "risky > safe", "ambiguity > non-ambiguous", or "hard > easy"). The task is a reinforcement learning paradigm with probabilistic feedback but no explicit manipulation or contrasts of risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty; therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (reward-based, involving uncertainty/ambiguity). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to decision-making (switch vs. stay) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps (Figures and text describe voxelwise random-effects t-scores). Whole-brain results are reported in figures and supported by supplementary analyses. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents that administered a risky decision-making task (economic lottery choice) during fMRI and modeled a parametric contrast of risk (coefficient of variation for chosen gambles; effectively high-risk > low-risk). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with FWE-corrected results and reported peak coordinates; Appendix B) in addition to ROI values, and describes task-evoked activation maps for the decision phase. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (whole-brain findings, statistics), and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing risky and ambiguous decision-making tasks. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses (activation maps, cluster correction) and provides tables of peak coordinates and contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > risk, SV parametric contrasts), satisfying the required contrasts and whole-brain reporting. The manuscript includes complete core content (methods, results, discussion) enabling extraction of whole-brain task activations. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an original human fMRI study in which participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task — a form of decision-making under uncertainty/ambiguity. The study reports within-task parametric contrasts (prediction error regressors across conditions and contrasts comparing reward-seeking vs. punishment-avoidance and face vs. abstract domains) that relate to probabilistic/uncertain decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (SPM random-effects) with reported coordinates and cluster-level inference, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Hence it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans using a Wheel-of-Fortune risky decision-making task (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risky decision-making (Risk vs. No-Risk; other probability/EV contrasts) (meets I5). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed with FLAME and cluster-correction; results are reported in tables/figures (meets I6 and I7). The full manuscript text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The article reports an empirical human fMRI study using a probabilistic monetary decision-making (risky-DM) task. It includes within-task contrasts/regressors relevant to risk/uncertainty (EV, RM/outcome, TD prediction error, reward variance/uncertainty) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with corrected peaks and coordinates (with figures/tables). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making), and thus involves a task-based fMRI scan during risky decisions. It includes task contrasts directly relevant to risky decision-making (risky > safe; punishment feedback > risky; and additional punished-then-risky and risky-then-risky contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses were conducted and reported (voxel-wise threshold P<0.001 with cluster correction; coordinates and cluster details provided), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting of results. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and are empirical task-evoked fMRI data. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human adults performing an adapted Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making) during scan (meets I4). The analysis includes within-task contrasts (active > passive decision blocks) directly related to risky/reward decision processing (meets I5). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (mixed-effects FLAME 1+2), with cluster-wise correction and figures/tables describing whole-brain results (meets I6 and I7). The article also contains methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), not only between-group contrasts without task maps (E5), and it is empirical with original fMRI data (not E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans performing a risk decision-making task (Gain/Loss gamble task) during scanning, meeting the review topic. The imaging analysis used SPM5 with whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial) including a parametric regressor for ‘Gamble Risk’ and reported voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) and SPM images/tables. Relevant within-task contrasts (e.g., Valence: Gain vs Loss; parametric risk: correlation with Gamble Risk) and between-group contrasts/interactions (ICD vs PD controls; Medication effects) are reported. The paper therefore satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (task-related contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). It does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging statistics).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (n=17) who performed a risky decision-making task (high- vs low-risk gambles). The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLM analyses testing task-related regressors (model-derived prediction error and difference-in-weights) and present statistical maps and activation foci (figures and Table 1). Results include between-subjects group one-sample t-tests and whole-brain thresholding; therefore the paper provides whole-brain task-evoked maps relevant to risky decision-making. It is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor non-empirical. All required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in young adults using a card-guessing task with explicit risky/uncertain reward conditions (possible win/loss/mixed/neutral), satisfying I4. The analyses include within-task contrasts and a parametric RE regressor tied to risk/uncertainty (and follow-up contrasts of win-anticipation vs neutral and loss-anticipation vs neutral), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM whole-brain multiple regression, FWE-corrected results, peak coordinates, and cluster reports) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying I6 and the permissive reporting format of I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes task-evoked whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This longitudinal fMRI study acquired task-evoked BOLD data while human participants performed the Paper-Scissors-Rock decision-making task with probabilistic (risky/uncertain) outcomes. The paper reports within-task contrasts (preferred/even/worst decision conditions) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses, with cluster-corrected significant activation maps and tabulated coordinates, satisfying reporting requirements. Methods describe whole-brain voxelwise PSC extraction, linear mixed-effects and regression analyses across a whole-brain mask, and corrected cluster thresholds; results present whole-brain group main effects and interactions. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human males performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a sequential risky decision-making task (meets I4). It provides within-task contrasts related to risk (parametric modulation of risk: green/risk balloon > orange/control balloon; cash > inflate contrasts) and decision-related contrasts (meets I5). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise GLMs using SPM8 with voxelwise FWE correction and reported peak coordinates and tables (meets I6 and I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and core analyses and coordinates are provided. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and whole-brain task effects are reported alongside interactions. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that acquired whole-brain BOLD data during decision-making tasks including a risky decision task (choices between safe and risky options) and a probabilistic reward task without learning. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical images (main effects displayed at uncorrected P<.001) and parametric within-task contrasts relating neural activity to expected value and reward prediction error (EV and RPE), which are relevant to risky decision-making. Although ROI analyses are reported for ventral striatum, whole-brain results are also presented and described. Therefore all inclusion criteria for risky/decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded: The fMRI paradigm involved repetitive value-preference choices between moral words (individualistic vs collectivistic), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s required task-domain criteria and is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic category learning (weather prediction) task involving decisions under uncertainty. The study reports task versus control contrasts (weather prediction > perceptual-motor control) and group × condition interactions. Imaging was analyzed with whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses, with voxelwise maps and coordinates reported (Table 3) and figures presenting main effects and contrasts. These elements satisfy: I4 (fMRI during a decision task under uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrast: experimental task > control task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, provides unmasked task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a difficult perceptual decision-making task (vertical vs. nonvertical Gabor discrimination) with trial-by-trial confidence ratings. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual uncertainty/decision-making (e.g., correct-sure > correct-unsure; correct > error) and analyzes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps using FSL/FLAME1 with cluster-based correction; results are presented as statistical maps, cluster tables, and figures.
