The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied.

This is a human fMRI study (N=15) in which participants performed a decision-making task (stop-the-clock RT task) manipulating uncertainty about reward outcomes. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric contrasts of relative uncertainty and mean uncertainty) with coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results, and present within-task contrasts examining high versus low uncertainty effects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=143) performing a risky decision-making task (gain/loss framing). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to risky decision-making (e.g., frame-consistent > frame-inconsistent; gamble vs safe), conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics, and provides/unthresholded group maps (NeuroVault). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a mixed gain–loss gambling task (risky decision-making) during scanning, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses reported (cluster- and voxel-wise results, coordinates, and correction). The paper reports within-task contrasts/modulations related to risk (linear and quadratic modulation of gain–loss ratios, sensitivity to extreme gambles) and between-group comparisons (gamblers vs controls). All inclusion criteria I4–I7 are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing incentivized probabilistic (risky) decision-making (Gambling blocks) and deterministic rule-based decisions. It reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to decision type and certainty (e.g., low vs high choice certainty probabilistic choices; probabilistic > rule and vice versa). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses were performed (one-sample t-tests on contrast images, SPM2) with results reported in tables/figures; ROI small-volume correction was used for some tests but whole-brain contrasts and group maps are described. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with volatile (high-uncertainty) and stable (low-uncertainty) decision-making phases. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing learning-rate modulation (volatile) versus nonlearning (stable) trials (psychological regressor = learning-rate trials vs nonlearning-rate trials), which maps onto the meta-analysis contrast class (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are presented (whole-brain thresholds, cluster correction, tables of coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not limited to ROI or connectivity-only results), is empirical, and includes the necessary contrasts. Hence it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task (meets I4). The paper includes within-task contrasts related to risk (parametric risk contrasts, win/loss outcomes, active-choice vs passive-no-choice) and reports correlations of brain activation with behavioral risk measures (meets I5). Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects models with cluster-level correction and report cluster results/tables (meets I6 and I7). The article contains full sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) and presents whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates; no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study acquired fMRI while human participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task), reported within-task parametric contrasts (pump number modulation of BOLD related to risk), and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses with cluster-corrected maps. Whole-brain results are described in the text and reported across regions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning (reinforcement-learning) task and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts (loseshift > winstay; final error > error). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is reinforcement/reversal learning, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis), I5 (no contrasts corresponding to risky vs safe, ambiguous vs unambiguous, or perceptual difficulty contrasts). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical limitations). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that used a decision-making task: subjects viewed multi-attribute objects and rated their combined value (decision behavior). The authors explicitly manipulated and decoded variability (high vs. low variability/ambiguity) and combined value, i.e., constructs directly relevant to ambiguous/risky/perceptual decision-making. Analyses produced group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps (time-resolved searchlight accuracy maps normalized to MNI space, second-level ANOVAs and voxelwise t-tests with cluster correction) and report coordinates and t-values for significant clusters (vmPFC, dlPFC, dmPC, cerebellum). Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/decoding of variability/ambiguity and value), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (reporting of coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Cups Task) during scanning, with within-subject contrasts comparing risky vs safe and EV-based contrasts (e.g., ADV Risk>DIS Risk). Analyses used whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM with cluster correction (FSL/FLAME; Z>2.3, p<.05 FWE) and reported significant regions and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task type, contrasts, whole-brain group-level analyses, and acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing risky decision-making tasks (choices between lotteries with shocks; regret/rejoice and probability-weighting tasks) while BOLD data were acquired. The paper reports task-related contrasts (e.g., probability-sensitive vs magnitude-sensitive activations; regret > rejoice and rejoice > regret patterns; voltage-weighted contrasts), group-level analyses, and whole-brain activation maps/tables described in the text and figures (Table 1, figures of regional activation). Thus it satisfies I4 (human fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision tasks), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported), and I7 (results presented as maps/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study acquired task-evoked BOLD data while human participants performed a probabilistic/uncertainty decision-making task (classical and modified beads tasks), which maps to ambiguous decision-making. It reports task contrasts relevant to ambiguity (lake decision > colour decision; last fish > all previous fish) at the group level. The authors performed and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction (tables/figures) and also present ROI analyses; whole-brain task effects are clearly described in the text and tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text is complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky/uncertainty decision-making task (BIAS), and presents within-task contrasts related to uncertainty and risk-avoidant vs risk-seeking choices (e.g., parametric modulation of uncertainty; bond vs stock choices). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported (thresholds, clusters, tables/figures referenced), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and GLM), results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study (N=94) in healthy adults that collected task-evoked BOLD responses while participants performed a monetary decision task (guessing High/Low) with gains and losses, meeting the review’s task domain. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., FB+ > FB− gain > loss) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster correction; results are reported in whole-brain tables/figures and described in the text. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of group-level whole-brain activation maps and contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Although this study uses fMRI and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not investigate the types of decision-making targeted by the meta-analysis. The task is a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) paradigm probing reward sensitivity and cognitive flexibility, and the reported contrasts are win-stay vs lose-stay (reward sensitivity) and lose-shift vs lose-stay (cognitive flexibility). These contrasts do not correspond to canonical risky (e.g., risky > safe), ambiguous (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous), or perceptual (e.g., hard > easy) decision-making contrasts required by I4 and I5. Therefore I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply, and the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that measured BOLD responses during a decision-making task (purchase intention ratings) and an explicit social risk rating task. The authors used within-task parametric modulators for social risk (high vs low social risk) and conducted group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction. Results are reported as whole-brain activations (tables/figures) linking social risk-related contrasts to activation (e.g., anterior insula, mPFC, TPJ). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task under uncertainty (two-choice prediction with explicit probabilities). It reports within-task contrasts (prediction > control; PdY−CtY, PdE−CtE, task-related and age-related contrasts) relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (SPM5) with cluster/FWE correction and activations reported in tables and figures (coordinates provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an olfactory two-alternative forced-choice perceptual decision-making task (open-sniff paradigm) with simultaneous fMRI acquisition (Experiment 2). The authors performed group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) correlating model-derived temporal integration profiles with fMRI time courses (one-sample t tests on subject-specific contrast images), yielding statistical parametric maps and reported activations (with small-volume correction for OFC). These contrasts directly probe perceptual decision-making (model-based integration; comparisons across trial difficulty and RT-related profiles). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task—an uncertain/ambiguous decision-making paradigm—meeting the review objective. It reports within-task regressors/contrasts tied to decision-making (expected value, positive/negative prediction errors, ambiguity/high vs low value) and relates these to behavior and group status. Analyses are voxelwise, whole-brain group-level maps with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic classification task that involves decision-making under uncertainty. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects second-level analyses) and contrasts directly related to ambiguity/uncertainty (parametric entropy regressor: increasing BOLD with increasing entropy/delay), which corresponds to ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Whole-brain statistical maps and corrected results are reported; results are presented in text/tables and ROI-confirmatory analyses do not replace the whole-brain outcomes. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults using a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney face detection) with within-task contrasts related to perception/decision (e.g., (DC+DR)>S, DR>DC, S>(DR+DC)). Analysis used group-level random-effects (RFX-GLM) whole-brain voxelwise maps and reports results in tables and figures. The paper includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing the Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making). The paper reports task contrasts relevant to risk (deck selection; advantageous vs disadvantageous decks) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (within-group whole-brain contrasts thresholded at z>2.3, p<.05 corrected). Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts relating to risky vs safe choices), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Full text reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing an economic decision task involving risk of detection for dishonest choices (risky decision-making). The study presents within-task contrasts comparing dishonest (risky) vs. honest (safe) choices (Dis–Hon) across detection conditions, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8; voxelwise p<0.001 with FWE cluster/peak correction) with MNI coordinates. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (relevant within-task contrast: Dis>Hon), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps), and I7 (coordinates and whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task to examine prediction-error signals and hippocampus–striatal interactions during reinforcement and incidental episodic encoding. It does NOT test risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined in the meta-analysis (no contrasts like risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). Inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I5 (at least one within-task/between-task contrast related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) are not met. The paper reports task-evoked fMRI and mentions whole-brain results, but the reported contrasts and ROIs focus on reinforcement prediction errors and memory, not risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision contrasts; therefore it does not qualify for this meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E6) are triggered by the available text.

Empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20) performing a probabilistic instrumental learning task with monetary rewards (25%/75%), i.e., decisions under risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to decision variables (state value, left/right option values, prediction errors) and contrasts comparing unequal vs equal reward probability pairs (behavioral learning effects). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, random-effects SPM voxelwise maps with reported coordinates and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement learning task with monetary gains and losses (240 trials with 70/30 contingencies). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to outcome processing (e.g., monetary gain vs neutral, loss vs neutral, gain omission, loss avoidance) and prediction-error parametric modulators, which are relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are conducted and reported (SPM8; whole-brain thresholds, cluster tables/coordinates are described). Results include whole-brain activation maps and coordinate-based tables rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only reports. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study used task fMRI while human participants performed the risky Iowa Gambling Task (satisfies I4) and reports a within-task contrast (IGT > control task) related to risky decision-making (satisfies I5). Results and coordinates are reported in text/figures (satisfies I7). However, all reported analyses were restricted to an anatomically defined VMPFC mask (ROI-based analyses); the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence). Hence the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary two-choice risk-taking task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., risky vs safe at cue/choice, risky win vs safe, risky win vs risky loss) and examines modulation by cumulative earnings. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (AFNI; cluster correction; coordinates reported in MNI/Talairach) with results presented in tables and figures. The full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Limitations) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task that manipulates uncertainty and reward contingencies (decision-making under probabilistic/ambiguous conditions). The paper reports within-task, task-evoked contrasts (trial-wise parametric modulators: learning rate, expected value, prediction error) and group-level voxelwise GLMs with reported activations (figures and cluster reports), and conducts whole-brain GLMs with small-volume correction in ROIs. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during decision-making under uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/risk), I6 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps produced), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants (adolescents) performing a decision-making task that explicitly manipulates risk and ambiguity (I4). Multiple within-task contrasts related to risky and ambiguous decision-making are reported (e.g., Risk Gamble > Ambiguity Gamble, Ambiguity Gamble > Risk Gamble, Gain > No Gain) meeting I5. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level statistics with Family Wise Error cluster correction and report coordinates in MNI space, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, participants, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and whole-brain contrasts), and Discussion; it is therefore complete and not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (anticipatory risk-choice task) satisfying the review objective. It reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., high-risk loss vs low-risk, feedback contrasts), and uses group-level random-effects analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported using familywise-error correction with identified clusters (whole-brain results and ROI follow-ups are included). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study meets I4 (task-based fMRI during human risky decision-making using an ecologically valid virtual ‘hook-up’ game) and I5 (it reports within-task contrasts such as SRD > implicit baseline and SRD > conversational). However, the group-level inference was conducted using TFCE permutation testing constrained to four a priori anatomical ROIs (insula, valuative, controlled-processing and impulsive regions). The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the primary SRD contrasts; the analyses and reported significant clusters are ROI-restricted. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map) is not satisfied. Consequently the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination of Gabor patches) while receiving rewards, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task voxelwise analyses related to perceptual decision difficulty and model-derived regressors (e.g., low vs high contrast trials, parametric correlates of predicted value and prediction error tied to stimulus discriminability), satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with reported statistical thresholds and peak MNI coordinates (FDR-corrected and uncorrected maps), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical fMRI data in healthy adults).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) during whole-brain, group-level analyses. The authors modeled parametric modulation of risk (probability of explosion) and tested within-task contrasts (risk covariation after wins vs losses) and a group × outcome interaction; results are reported from voxelwise whole-brain second-level (random-effects) analyses with multiple-comparison correction. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study tested healthy human participants performing 2- and 4-choice reversal learning tasks that directly manipulate outcome certainty/uncertainty for future choices. The authors report within-subject contrasts comparing uncertain versus certain outcomes (4-choice > 2-choice for unexpected non-reinforcement vs expected reinforcement) that map onto ambiguous/uncertain decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (FSL, Z-thresholding, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures/tables provided. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (within-/between-task contrast related to uncertainty/ambiguity), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I7 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that directly examines decision making under risk using explicit probabilities and incentives. The methods report task-based fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, voxelwise individual- and group-level (second-level random-effects) analyses using SPM2, whole-brain corrections, and reported peak coordinates and cluster tables. Relevant contrasts related to risky decision-making are present (activation condition A versus high-level control B; A versus C), matching experimental-task > control-task contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps (voxelwise analyses) with coordinates in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI meta-analysis of risky decision-making.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses were performed and reported) and I7 (whole-brain results are described in the text/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5. The task used is a reward-processing High/Low Card Guessing Task that the authors explicitly state does not constitute risky decision-making; it is not framed or analyzed as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. The contrasts reported (reward vs. no-reward; anticipation vs. receipt of reward) are reward-processing contrasts, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts required by I4/I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis even though whole-brain analyses were conducted.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) with task contrasts (motivated > neutral; stimulus/decision events vs baseline) reported at the group level. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain FWE-corrected results) and also reports contrasts in tables/ROIs; thus it meets the requirement for whole-brain group-level maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria E3–E6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (N=24 included) who performed a decision-making task involving risk/uncertainty (a limited-offer paradigm where subjects choose to accept or wait with probabilistic withdrawal/high-offer outcomes). Task contrasts and model-based regressors relate directly to decision uncertainty/precision and choice conflict (analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty contrasts). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects), corrected results, and tables/figures of whole-brain effects as well as ROI checks. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing two decision-making tasks (IGT and RDT) that probe risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts relevant to risk/ambiguity (e.g., parametrically modeled reward PE and risk PE regressors, and the IGT > RDT contrast for updating predictions). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLMs with familywise-error cluster correction and results reported in figures/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (supplemental material noted but not required). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not solely between-group without task effects, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (skewed gambling), meeting I4. It reports within-task contrasts related to risk (skewed vs symmetric; positive vs negative skew) and trial-level regressions predicting acceptance, meeting I5. The paper performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise thresholding, cluster correction using AFNI’s 3dFWHMx/3dClustSim) and reports significant clusters and tables/figures of whole-brain results, meeting I6 and satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, and include unmasked whole-brain task activation maps. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the fMRI component does not meet the review’s decision-making criteria and reports only ROI-based activation. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (study reports ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none ([]). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was conducted during a Monetary Incentive Delay task probing reward responses, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review), I5 (contrasts reported are win vs no-win outcomes rather than contrasts indexing risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or hard vs easy perceptual decisions), and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported; analyses extract ROI beta weights from basal ganglia). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) during scanning, satisfying I4. It reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., task blocks contrasted with baseline and motivated > neutral contrasts such as NEGATIVE > NEUTRAL, POSITIVE > NEUTRAL), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level repeated-measures ANOVA) with FWE-corrected whole-brain results and tables of coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This empirical fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps while human participants performed a decision-making task under maximum uncertainty (50% contingency). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguous decision-making (50% probability condition vs implicit baseline), group-level one-way ANOVA voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) and tables/figures with coordinates. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making tasks (spatial and shape comparisons). Task contrasts include spatial-comparison > target-detection baseline and comparisons between ‘within’ vs ‘between’ image tasks (manipulating difficulty), fitting perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., hard>easy / task>control). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects maps (projected to inflated cortex) and reported whole-brain results in the text/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) during BOLD scanning. The authors report task-related contrasts based on a trial-by-trial prediction-error regressor (a within-task, decision-related parametric contrast). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (two-sample t tests with cluster correction; significant clusters listed in Table 2 and shown in Figure 2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Results are reported in the main text, tables, and figures. The study is not ROI-only, not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, and is empirical with original task-evoked activation maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI investigation of reinforcement-learning (reward/punishment) using a probabilistic instrumental learning task. While it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and prediction-error contrasts (satisfying I6), it does not investigate risky decision-making (risk vs safe), ambiguity/uncertainty contrasts, or perceptual decision difficulty contrasts as required by the review objectives. Specifically, there are no contrasts of the form “risky > safe”, “ambiguity > non-ambiguity”, or “hard > easy” (I4 and I5 are not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the targeted risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making domains despite meeting whole-brain reporting requirements.

This empirical fMRI study acquired task-related whole-brain fMRI while healthy human participants performed a probabilistic decision-making task in which risk was explicitly modeled. The authors report within-task, task-evoked contrasts/parametric modulators related to risk prediction (and reward prediction/difficulty), tested at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise GLM with multiple-comparison correction, and report the resulting activations and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/reward (Win > No Win) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses (task activation-masked ANCOVA and whole-brain results with voxel- and cluster-level correction) with tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and processing), Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked whole-brain maps, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is excluded because it does not provide a within-task or between-task contrast that specifically indexes risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis (I5 not met). The paper reports an event-related probabilistic reversal learning task (fMRI in humans) and group-level whole-brain activation maps with coordinate tables (I4, I6, I7 are satisfied), but the critical contrast used (‘final reversal error vs baseline’) reflects reversal-learning processes and not explicit risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI in human participants who performed both an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma and an explicit gamble (risky) task. It includes within-task contrasts for the gamble outcomes ($0, $1, $2) and uses a ($0-$2) contrast representing unsuccessful vs successful gamble outcomes; it further reports a task-by-payoff interaction ((CD-CC)-($0-$2)) directly comparing social and non-social (risky) decision outcomes. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects maps (thresholds and cluster extents reported), with results presented in tables and figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports an event-related fMRI in healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task). It includes a within-task contrast of interest (risky decisions minus safe decisions) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical parametric maps with voxelwise thresholds and corrected peaks (coordinates and figures provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for task-evoked whole-brain fMRI of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a mixed-gambling risky decision-making task (variable win/loss amounts and win probability). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8) with parametric contrasts related to risk and value (e.g., EV, k_WIN, k_LOSE, p, |p-0.5|, EV/〈k〉, Var), cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinate-based tables/figures. Results include whole-brain maps and corrected clusters (Table 2, figures), satisfying voxelwise reporting. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with within-task contrasts comparing reward vs nonreward and decision-period contrasts (e.g., R75/25 vs NR75/25; res-R75 vs res-NR75). The analysis is group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (GLM, random-effects), with reported peak coordinates and multiple-comparison corrections (FDR and cluster thresholds), meeting the requirement that whole-brain results are available in tables/figures/text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study of causal one-shot learning (passive stimulus–outcome observation with post-hoc causal ratings), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Although the study reports group-level whole-brain activation maps and figures (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not involve participants performing risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I4 not met) and does not report within-task contrasts of the types required for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy) (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

The study used task-based fMRI and reports whole-brain analyses, but the in-scanner task (card guessing) and reported contrasts focus on reward outcome (win>loss, FB+>FB−, and their interaction) rather than contrasts that index risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Thus it does not provide within-task or between-task contrasts directly related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making required by I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no contrast specifically indexing risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making in the fMRI task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task (trial-wise probabilistic rewards), i.e., an uncertainty/risk-related decision-making task (meets I4). The authors report within-task parametric contrasts of reward prediction errors (RPEs) at the time of feedback and group comparisons based on these task-evoked effects (meets I5). Second-level, group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are described (main effect of RPEs with voxel-height FWE p<.05; group comparisons with cluster-extent FWE correction), indicating voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (meets I6). Results are described in the main text with supplementary figures/tables referenced (meets I7). The study is empirical with whole-brain task activation results; it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor non-empirical, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's decision-making task requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task does not require participants to perform risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making – spins were automatic and participants did not make choices between risk levels), and I5 (no contrasts reflecting decision-making under risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty such as “risky>safe”, “high-risk>low-risk”, or “hard>easy”; reported contrasts are wins vs losses and large vs small wins, which index outcome processing rather than decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (N=15) performing a tactile perceptual decision-making task (pattern orientation discrimination) with both immediate and delayed response conditions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and identifies task-related regions with significant parametric modulation by decision difficulty (i.e., hard > easy effects implemented via parametric modulation of reaction times), satisfying the requirement for within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (thresholded, corrected maps and ROI derivation from these maps) and figures/tables describe the findings. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports task-based fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task), with a within-task parametric contrast of risk level (risk-related pumps). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (one-sample t-test with family-wise error cluster correction) reporting activated regions. Thus it meets I4 (task fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast related to risk level), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I7 (results clearly described). Although the paper also includes resting-state connectivity analyses, it additionally provides unmasked whole-brain task activation results, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports simultaneous fMRI acquisition while human participants performed decision-making tasks that explicitly include uncertainty (explicit probability levels) and reward/cost tradeoffs (i.e., risky decision-making), satisfying I4. The authors performed within-task contrasts (each task vs control) and derived activation t-maps/GLMs, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported and illustrated (e.g., Fig. 8; thresholded maps, jICA fMRI components), satisfying I6 and the acceptable reporting formats in I7. The manuscript provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical), so exclusion_criteria_applied is []. Accordingly, this study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling task that probes risky decision-making (meets review domain). The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses relating previous outcomes to risky vs. non-risky choices and presents group-level random-effects voxelwise whole-brain analyses, conjunctions, tables of coordinates, and figures. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/risky vs non-risky), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing an investing paradigm explicitly contrasting risky (stock) vs safe (bond) choices (meets I4). It includes within-task contrasts directly related to risky decision-making (e.g., stock > bond in the gain domain) and other task contrasts (meets I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (e.g., whole-brain RPE activation with FWE correction) and group-level SPM files/contrast maps are available in the data repository (meets I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; not between-groups-only without unmasked task effect; empirical original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used a loss-aversion economic gamble task (risky decision-making) during scanning. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts for gain- and loss-related BOLD responses and group ANOVAs (e.g., gain-weighted and loss-weighted activation contrasts), satisfying a within-task/task-related contrast. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps with cluster correction and reported thresholding/tables/figures. Results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and tables/figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain evidence and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that used fMRI while participants performed an experiential risky decision-making task (choices between sure and risky monetary options). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., analyses of 20¢ vs 0/40¢ choices and contrasts of risk trials vs others) and conducts a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis using SPM2 with familywise error correction; results are reported in a table of clusters (Table 1) and supplemental figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (task fMRI of risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task in the scanner (ambiguous cue conditioning; obtain-reward vs avoid-punishment choices). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguity (factor tone ANOVA; parametric linear modulation across NT->PT and quadratic/reverse-quadratic tests capturing ambiguity-related effects, including a reverse U trend for ambiguous stimuli), and a learned valence contrast (PT vs NT). Analyses are group-level whole-brain SPM8 voxelwise results (FWE cluster-corrected), with tables/figures of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a two-choice prediction task manipulating outcome uncertainty (50% vs 20%/80% error rates). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (AFNI, voxelwise percent signal change, cluster correction) and explicit contrasts addressing ambiguity/uncertainty (e.g., 50% > ½(20%+80%)) as well as task>control contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain activation maps and Talairach-coordinates/tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs) is included. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and whole-brain task effects are reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies and should be included.

The manuscript reports an fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) (I4). It includes within-task contrasts of interest (risky vs. safe selections) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (AFNI 3dANOVA3, AlphaSim correction) with clusters and peak coordinates presented (I6, I7). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a sequential gambling task (risk-taking). The paper reports within-task, task-evoked contrasts and parametric modulators directly related to risk (e.g., cumulative gambling/accumulated sum, stop probability) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported statistical maps and tables of coordinates (second-level one-sample t tests, thresholding and cluster correction). Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides whole-brain results suitable for coordinate-based or image-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports BOLD fMRI in human participants performing decision-making tasks (delay discounting and risk sensitivity) during scanning, includes within-task contrasts (choice vs baseline; parametric subjective value; categorical choice regressors), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses thresholded and cluster-corrected using permutation testing. Results are described in the main text and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study with healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (accept/reject mixed monetary gambles) while scanned (3T fMRI), satisfying I4. The authors report within-task, task-evoked contrasts related to risk/loss processing (parametric contrasts of prospective gains vs losses, losses>gains, bidirectional responses, acceptance>rejection), satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 results with voxel- and cluster-level corrections and tables/figures reporting coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor non-empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making task (accept/reject 50:50 gambles) with imaging acquired during task performance. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (novel vs familiar prime) modeled at the group level and relates these contrasts to percent risky choices via second-level regression; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses were performed and peak coordinates/clusters (hippocampus, putamen) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study used fMRI during passive tactile texture stimulation, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore it does not provide within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. It does report group-level whole-brain task activation maps and presents results in tables/figures. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion not met: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making-related contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full-text reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans performing a gambling decision-making task manipulating reward uncertainty (risk/ambiguity). The paper includes within-task contrasts related to uncertainty and outcome (e.g., uncertain > probable, probable win > probable loss) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and exploratory whole-brain contrasts (z-maps, coordinates/figures). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies: (I4) participants performed a probability-discounting (risky decision-making) task during fMRI; (I5) within-task contrasts related to risk (probabilistic > fixed choices) and a between-group contrast ((IGD_probabilistic − IGD_fixed) − (HC_probabilistic − HC_fixed)) are reported; (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted in SPM with cluster-level FWE correction (AlphaSim) and reported coordinates; (I7) whole-brain results are described in the text and reported in tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include whole-brain task activation maps rather than only between-group interactions without unmasked task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that administered a decision-making task (modified Ultimatum Game) during scanning. The task includes choices between fair (safer) and slightly selfish (riskier) offers, and the paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risk-related decision-making (e.g., slightly selfish > fair and fair > selfish). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM with reported activation clusters and thresholding; results and peak coordinates are described in the text/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study used whole-brain fMRI and reported group-level voxelwise task activation maps (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is an erotic Go/NoGo response-inhibition paradigm (motivational salience), not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. The primary contrasts are NoGo > Go, Male > Female, and motivationally-relevant inhibition — none correspond to typical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts (e.g., risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, hard > easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply and the full text appears complete.

This empirical study performed fMRI while human adolescents completed a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game), satisfying I4. It reports within-task contrasts isolating decision-related activity (Decision Trial – Directed Trial), and analyzes deliberation periods separately for risky and cautious responses, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses were conducted using SPM8 with cluster-level FWE correction and results presented as statistical maps and tables of coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, task-effect absent, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a multi-cue probabilistic classification task (decision-making under uncertainty). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to decision evidence/uncertainty (parametric modulation by subjective and objective Sum-of-Evidence, comparisons of low vs. high time pressure), i.e., ambiguity/uncertainty and hard>easy–type effects. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (searchlight SVR, GLMs, one-sample t-tests, whole-brain cluster correction) with tables and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing an ambiguous decision-making task (odd/even with certain vs uncertain trials). It reports within-task contrasts (uncertain > certain) and between-group comparisons, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (thresholds and cluster extents reported; tables/figures described). The full text includes introduction, methods (task, acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results (whole-brain activations and connectivity), and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast related to ambiguity: uncertain>certain), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not only connectivity/resting-state; includes within-task whole-brain effects; is empirical). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study examined probabilistic classification learning using informational feedback (category learning), not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined for the review. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps were reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in the text/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the task is category-learning with cognitive feedback, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm) and I5 (no within- or between-task contrasts explicitly indexed risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty; contrasts relate to prediction error and feedback valence). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it does not meet the core task-related inclusion criteria I4 and I5.

The study meets I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I5 (reports risky > safe contrasts). However, it does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map (I6 not met). The report relies on ROI analyses (Table 2, MarsBaR percent signal changes) and between-group ROI contrasts; no whole-brain, group-level task maps or unmasked voxelwise results are presented. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results) and E5 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete. Given these missing whole-brain group-level results, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI monetary decision-making task with contrasts of risky > safe and thus meets I4 (task fMRI of risky decision-making) and I5 (within-task contrast risky>safe). However, the imaging analysis and results are reported using restricted a priori ROI voxel-wise tests (OFC/VLPFC, ACC, etc.) and small-volume corrected peaks; no group-level, whole-brain (unrestricted voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain coordinate results are presented. Therefore it does not meet I6 and falls under exclusion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task with explicit risky vs safe (A+B vs C+D) and decision-making vs control contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 with random-effects one-sample t-tests, and results are reported as whole-brain clusters and peak coordinates (tables/figures). The manuscript therefore satisfies I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (risky>safe and other within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), and I7 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task), meeting I4. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts tied to risk (e.g., ChooseInflate*P(explode), ChooseWin*P(explode)) and related contrasts, meeting I5. Analyses were conducted at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain GLMs in SPM5 with FDR and cluster corrections and second-level whole-brain tests, satisfying I6; results are reported in the text and figures, satisfying I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical primary data present). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that acquired task-evoked BOLD during a gambling task involving explicit risk (reward, punishment, neutral trials). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reward>neutral, loss>neutral) and group/covariate analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed using SPM8 with FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates provided. Reporting includes whole-brain activation maps/tables (not ROI-only), satisfying the review’s requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are met. Full text content is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly, the study meets I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), which is a standard risky decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risk decisions following negative versus positive feedback (e.g., risk taking post-explosion > post-cash-out), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, reporting coordinates and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and whole-brain GLM), results (behavioral and whole-brain results), and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (within-task contrast related to risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of value/salience using a noninstrumental outcome-prediction task with deterministic appetitive and aversive monetary outcomes (gains/losses). It does not involve risky (probabilistic) or ambiguous decision-making nor a perceptual difficulty/manipulation. Therefore it does not meet I4 (task must be a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and does not provide any within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual decision difficulty required by I5. The manuscript does provide group-level, voxelwise whole-brain information maps from searchlight MVPA (group one-sample t tests on accuracy maps) and reports coordinates/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I4 and I5 are not met; inclusion criteria satisfied: [I6, I7]; inclusion criteria not met: [I4, I5]; exclusion criteria met: []

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that implements a risky decision-making task (modified Stoplight driving game) during BOLD fMRI, satisfying I4. It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk (e.g., Go > Stop; Pass > Crash) and group comparisons, satisfying I5. Analysis was conducted at the group (second) level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 analyses with FWE correction and reports peak coordinates and whole-brain results in text/figures/tables, satisfying I6 and I7. The paper includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adults (cognitively normal older adults) performing a lottery choice task that manipulates risk via probabilities and magnitudes (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task parametric contrasts of expected value (EV) during choice and gain/loss feedback contrasts, and they conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (voxel thresholds, cluster correction) and provide peak coordinate tables. Thus it satisfies fMRI task requirement (I4), within-task contrasts related to risk/Ev (I5), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (I6), and reporting of results in tables/figures (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that includes a probability discounting (risky decision-making) task and an intertemporal task. It reports within-task contrasts (free vs. forced choice) tied to decision-making under risk and presents group-level, whole-brain (random-effects, second-level) analyses with tables of peak coordinates and appropriate thresholds (including whole-brain FWE-corrected results). Therefore it satisfies the review’s requirements for task type, relevant contrasts, whole-brain group maps, and acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

Empirical fMRI study in humans performing monetary decision-making with risky, ambiguous, and certain gambles; reports within-task contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > risk; risk > certain) and correlates of preference parameters; uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analysis with SPM and reports cluster thresholds and coordinates. Full article contains Introduction, Methods (imaging and behavioral), Results, and Discussion. Not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, and is empirical. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky and ambiguous decision-making.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (risky-gains), with within-task contrasts (risky > safe) and group comparisons. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (one-sample and two-sample t-tests, voxel-wise threshold P<0.001 uncorrected and cluster extent threshold) and display t-maps and region labels; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present. Full paper contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and limitations; full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) during scanning, directly manipulating risk and agency (meets I4). The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts related to risk (parametric risk regressors, active vs passive contrasts; meets I5). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM random-effects results with whole-brain FDR correction and reported coordinate tables/figures (meets I6 and I7). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using the Colorado Balloon Game, a risky decision-making task conducted during fMRI. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (Decision-Balloon vs Directed-Balloon; DecBa-minus-DirBa for decision, wins, and losses) directly related to risky decision-making, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with voxel- and cluster-level FWE correction, including tables/figures of activation loci. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging acquisition, whole-brain analysis), Results (within-group and between-group whole-brain contrasts), and Discussion, so the full article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a sequential risk-taking (decision-making) task during scanning. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to risky outcomes (e.g., Gain vs Loss, Context (Self vs Computer) × Outcome (Optimum, Non-optimum, Devil), parametric regressors for obtained gain, missed chances, and lost coins) and conducts group-level, second-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial in SPM8) with reported MNI coordinates and thresholding. Results are reported whole-brain (tables/coordinates/figures). Thus, it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that acquired task-based whole-brain functional images while participants performed risk-related driving tasks (urgent braking vs evaluative risk judgments). The paper reports within-task contrasts (urgent > evaluative and evaluative > urgent) that directly index risk-related decision processes, and presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster coordinates and statistical thresholds (Table 1, figures) consistent with inclusion. The manuscript includes full methods, preprocessing, first- and second-level analyses, and corrected whole-brain activation maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of sequential predictive learning (serial reaction time), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Although it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and supplementary cluster tables (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not report within-task contrasts that map onto risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, risk>safe). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (and I4 is not clearly met because the task is not a perceptual decision-making paradigm of the type targeted by this review).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans (n=23) that implemented perceptual decision-making tasks (emotion discrimination and gender discrimination on faces). It reports within-task and between-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (emotion > control, gender > control, emotion > gender) and includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables of coordinates. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual detection decision-making task (animal detection) with manipulation of motivational context. It reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (Pos > Neut-P and Neg > Neut-N) and examines their relationship to behavior. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholds, FWE correction, cluster extent) and reports coordinate-based results; ROI analyses are present but do not replace whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (coherent motion discrimination) with manipulated difficulty (coherence) and stimulus duration. It reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (effects of low vs high coherence; short vs long duration) and computes group-level analyses beyond ROI work (the paper describes group-level voxelwise analyses and reports whole-brain thresholded effects). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext is complete. Inclusion criteria I4 (task fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/coherence), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses performed), and I7 (whole-brain results described in text/figures at voxelwise thresholds) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study meets all fMRI meta-analysis inclusion requirements: (I4) participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task during simultaneous fMRI (task with explicit reward probabilities 0.8/0.2 — decision under risk/uncertainty); (I5) the authors report within-task parametric contrasts related to reward prediction errors (RPEcue and RPEoutcome) tied to decision-making and learning; (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded (cluster-extent FWE correction) with reported clusters/coordinates; (I7) whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a probabilistic reversal-learning (reward-based decision-making) task, which constitutes decision-making under probabilistic (risky) contingencies.
