The study reports multiple within-task contrasts (e.g., negative feedback > positive feedback; final reversal error vs. reversal error; final reversal error vs. correct responses) that index reward-based decision processes and adaptive choice behavior. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM models (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) with whole-brain FWE correction and reported coordinates/activations, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (mixed lotteries) during scanning, meeting the review objective. It reports task-related within-subject parametric contrasts for gains and losses and contrasts of gains > losses and vice versa. Group-level, voxelwise (second-level) analyses were performed; the manuscript reports ROI analyses with small-volume correction but also states whole-brain and exploratory analyses and whole-brain FWE-corrected within-group results are reported in the supplementary figures/tables, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without task effects, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making (difference judgment) tasks across visual and auditory modalities. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing judgment versus passive viewing/blank (perceptual task > control), includes group-level mixed-effects analyses of functional data using FSL, presents whole-brain voxelwise results (figures and Talairach coordinates/table), and provides adequate methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (perceptual task > control contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (coordinates/figures reporting whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains), with voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses and reported contrasts directly related to risk (e.g., risky > safe; risky responses > punished trials). Results are presented as thresholded statistical maps and tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task contrasts). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual categorization (radial vs concentric Glass patterns) decision-making task with parametric stimulus difficulty and learned-category manipulations. It reports within-task comparisons related to perceptual decisions (classification of radial vs concentric choices; analyses of stimuli near the category boundary and learning-induced shifts), satisfying the perceptual decision-making contrasts requirement. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from a multivoxel searchlight analysis and second-level statistical tests (t tests, cluster thresholds) identifying voxels with above-chance classification accuracy, fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting; results are described in the main text and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and experimental procedures and appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (N=21) conducting a risky decision-making task with monetary gambles. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (random-effects) and presents whole-brain activation results (Tables and figures) for contrasts related to probability and nonlinear weighting (parametric modulators p·u(x) and Δ(p)·u(x)), as well as nonparametric analyses. The study is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI experiment in healthy humans performing a probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making task (Jumping-to-Conclusions) and includes within-task comparisons of task stages via multivariate analyses (I4 and I5 met). However, all reported analyses are ROI-based (predefined PFC and temporal ROIs) and voxel-selection within those ROIs; no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures are reported. Therefore it does not meet I6. Exclusion E3 applies (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study reports event-related fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision under probabilistic/uncertain outcomes), meeting I4 (task involves probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making). It includes within-task contrasts comparing punished (probabilistic error) versus rewarded correct responses, satisfying I5. Analyses are voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain with cluster-level FWE correction and reported clusters/coordinates and figures, meeting I6 and I7. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) that probes risk under uncertainty. The paper reports a within-task contrast directly relevant to risky decision-making (risky > safe) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and between-group comparisons) with results described and thresholding procedures reported. Whole-brain results are presented (including that there were few significant clusters) and functional ROI analyses are supplementary to the whole-brain approach. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical, within-subject, double-blind, placebo-controlled fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed a gambling/guessing task with uncertain (risky/ambiguous) outcomes. The paper reports within-task contrasts that compare anticipation of reward (e.g., Ant $4 – No-change $4; Ant 50c – No-ch 50c), appropriate for risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts. Analyses were voxel-wise, second-level group (flexible factorial) whole-brain comparisons with reported clusters and coordinates (voxelwise threshold p<0.001, cluster extent), and results are described in the text/tables/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, non-empirical, or only between-group without task maps) are met. Accordingly, the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty). The paper reports task-related within-subject contrasts (reversal switch errors vs baseline; nonswitch/probabilistic errors vs baseline) that index processing of probabilistic/ambiguous feedback. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported with coordinates and corrected p-values (e.g., dorsomedial PFC at x=9,y=39,z=48; Pcorrected=0.006), and results are described in the main text and tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

(a) Exclusion met: E3 - the study reports primarily ROI analyses focused on the amygdala and used a limited field-of-view (four functional slices centered on the amygdala), so it does not provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map. Although a group GLM is reported, coverage and focus are restricted to the amygdala. (b) Inclusion met: I4 - human fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (interactive domino bluffing); I5 - within-task contrasts related to risk (nonmatch (risky) vs match (safe) and show vs no-show contrasts). (c) Inclusion not met: I6 - does not provide whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps due to limited slice coverage and ROI emphasis. I7 not applicable. Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task with within-task comparisons of cue conditions (random-dot motion task), so it satisfies I4 (fMRI with human perceptual DM) and I5 (within-task contrast related to perceptual decision-making). However, the paper reports ROI-based reconstruction and region-specific analyses (V1, V2, etc.) and does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain activation contrasts. Therefore it fails I6 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

While the study reports fMRI during human choices between risky and ambiguous lotteries and voxelwise analyses linked to subjective value (meets I4 and I5), the full text presents only single-subject activation maps and methodological guidance. It does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or provide group coordinates/tables clearly described in the text. Thus I6 (group-level whole-brain evidence) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) but lacks the required group-level whole-brain results for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is a simultaneous EEG–fMRI empirical study in healthy adults performing a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under probabilistic uncertainty). The authors report within-task parametric fMRI analyses linked to signed and absolute reward prediction errors (sRPE, |RPE|), including group-level, whole-brain (SPM8) random-effects analyses with cluster correction and reported peaks/tables/figures. These contrasts directly index uncertainty/surprise-related decision-making (analogous to “high uncertainty > low uncertainty” or parametric |RPE| effects). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplementary material available). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not non-empirical, and includes task activation maps). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed a perceptual decision-making task (face gender categorization) during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision making (e.g., noise-present > noise-absent, noise-present > control; analogous to low-coherence > high-coherence) and explicitly conducts whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates (Table 1) and conjunctions. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (50/69/100%) reinforcement-learning task that manipulates predictability/uncertainty. The authors report within-task contrasts directly addressing uncertainty/predictability (e.g., 100%<69%<50%), which map onto ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (SPM5 second-level analyses) with coordinates/tables and figures reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI study of ambiguous decision-making with whole-brain task-evoked maps and reported contrasts/coordinates.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (near-threshold pain detection) with an experimental threat manipulation. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decisions (e.g., pain > no pain; high threat > low threat) and performs group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level SPM analyses with reported coordinates and statistical thresholds. Thus it satisfies I4 (human fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decisions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that used a lottery-choice (mixed-lottery) decision-making task (risky decisions) during task fMRI, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts and model-based regressors related to probability/magnitude/EV and age × probability effects, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (first-level to group-level ANOVA and model-based whole-brain t-tests) are described with clusterwise thresholds and reported results/tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplementary tables are referenced; no exclusion criteria apply. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making whole-brain fMRI data.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky/ probabilistic decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It reports within-task contrasts (decision trials (money) > control; win > no-win) and between-condition contrasts (abstinent vs satiated) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FEAT) with cluster correction; results are reported in tables, figures, and text. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (direction-of-motion discrimination). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (high-coherence > low-coherence and low > high coherence), and additional contrasts (response modality effects). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise mixed-effects GLM with cluster-based thresholding; coordinates and tables of activations are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a Paper-Scissors-Rock reinforcement-learning task (decision-making under probabilistic uncertainty). The authors report within-task contrasts relevant to decision uncertainty and outcome valence (early trials vs late trials reflecting higher vs lower uncertainty; outcome contrasts wins/ties/losses), satisfying the requirement for risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (AFNI whole-brain GLM, Monte-Carlo cluster correction) with coordinates and cluster tables described in the text, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are presented as group-level whole-brain maps and coordinate tables, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be included.

The study acquired fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty) and an emotional picture viewing task. It includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to decision-making (reward > punishment in post-PE/post-reversal trials) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical maps (group-level contrasts and whole-brain checks are described, with coordinates provided for significant clusters). Although some results were tested within a ventral striatum ROI, the paper also reports group-level whole-brain analyses (and explicitly notes when effects did not survive whole-brain correction). Reporting includes coordinates and permutation-corrected statistics. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults using the Iowa Gambling Task (an ambiguous risky decision-making paradigm) acquired with BOLD fMRI. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity (disadvantageous > advantageous; advantageous > disadvantageous; win > loss; loss > win; and EV-modulated contrasts) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (XBAM permutation-based cluster inference) with cluster tables and figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (relevant within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in maps/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing an ambiguous/risky decision-making task (learning and experiment proper). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguity/second-order uncertainty (e.g., ambiguous > nonambiguous; parametric effects of entropy) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM, reporting cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral, model comparison, fMRI results) and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task with stochastic rewards/punishments (70/30 and 40/60 schedules), constituting a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds, and includes task-related contrasts/regressors relevant to decision-making (model-derived prior correct, posterior–prior update, switch>stay, and model comparisons vs RL). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text is considered complete.

The study is an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (ring-size discrimination), so it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI in perceptual decision-making) and I5 (within-task contrasts comparing stimulus/choice conditions). However, the analyses are confined to V1 (retinotopically defined ROI) and population analyses within that ROI; the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or whole-brain coordinates for task effects. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Based on these factors, I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a probabilistic association learning (Weather Prediction Task), which involves decision-making under uncertainty. It includes within-task contrasts (weather prediction task > perceptual-motor control) and group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with figures and coordinate tables (Supplementary Table S2). Thus the paper provides a group-level, whole-brain task activation map relevant to decision-making under uncertainty. All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI or connectivity/resting-state results, and it is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used event-related fMRI in healthy humans and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is probabilistic reversal learning (feedback-based learning/flexibility), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (does not satisfy I4). The reported contrasts (e.g., final reversal errors − nonswitch errors; nonswitch errors − correct responses) do not correspond to risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision contrasts (does not satisfy I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore, exclude because key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (3D heading discrimination), fulfilling I4. It includes within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (EASY > HARD; COH and FOE manipulations; conjunction analyses), fulfilling I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (random-effects second-level t-tests, thresholded maps, conjunction), fulfilling I6, and results are reported in maps/tables and described in text, fulfilling I7. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a card gambling task (risky decision-making). The manuscript reports within-task, within-subject and between-condition contrasts related to risk level (six risk levels, negative vs positive outcomes, low-risk vs high-risk), and tests interactions between pharmacological challenge and risk level. Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise statistics using SPM5 with cluster-level FWE correction and report stereotactic coordinates and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/ resting-only, not non-empirical, and includes whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study satisfies I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a lottery choice task involving risk (choices between lotteries with different expected value and risk), satisfying the review scope. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to decision-making under risk (e.g., main effects of valence, outcome context, interactions between outcome context and valence, and choice-period contrasts such as social > private) derived from a whole-brain GLM. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (SPM5, voxel-wise FDR correction), and coordinates/activation maps and tables are provided. The study is not ROI-only, not solely connectivity-based, and is an original empirical report. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study used an intertemporal delay-discounting (value-based) task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrast reported: hard>easy), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses reported), I7 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task domain = delay discounting/intertemporal choice, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion; up vs. down) with event-related trial structure and behavioral calibration. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (analyses across motion coherence levels; hard/low-coherence vs easy/high-coherence comparisons; parametric regressors of coherence) and multivariate choice-decoding analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (group repeated-measures ANOVAs, group t-tests, searchlight maps, and tables/coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group-only; empirical data present). Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion direction discrimination) with manipulations of motion coherence, response modality, and foreknowledge. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., low coherence > high coherence) and uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (GLM, permutation tests, group maps, cluster correction) presented in figures and text. Thus it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study manipulated predictability of image location and semantic category during passive viewing/implicit learning, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Although group-level, whole-brain task activation maps are reported (satisfying I6) and results are presented in figures/tables (satisfying I7), the experiment did not require participants to perform perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence) nor risky/ambiguous choices. Therefore I4 (task was a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (Talairach coordinates/clusters). However, the reported primary imaging contrasts analyzed in the paper focus on reward feedback (Win vs. No Win) rather than a decision-related contrast indexing risk or ambiguity (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or ambiguous > non-ambiguous). Although selection-phase regressors were modeled, the published results and group-level maps presented here are limited to the feedback (outcome) contrast; no whole-brain decision-making (risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty) contrasts are reported in the full text. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one within-task or between-task contrast related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) is not met, while I4, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case fMRI study (n=1) that acquired task-evoked BOLD data during a decision-making task and reports within-task contrasts (A>B) with coordinate tables; however the meta-analysis requires group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. The study does not present group-level whole-brain results (inclusion criterion I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (task fMRI during decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast related to risky decision-making), I7 (reports coordinates/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making task (probability discounting) during scanning. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts related to risk (subjective value of risky option, chosen value, decision conflict) and categorical task effects, with group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps, coordinates, and SPM results; ROI corrections reported but whole-brain results are present). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical pharmacological fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a monetary decision-making task with explicit risky vs less risky choices (bet £1 vs 10p) and probabilistic contingencies. The authors report task-based, group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses identifying neural correlates of choice temperature (a risk-related/decision stochasticity variable) and learning rate, including one-sample whole-brain tests (placebo) and paired whole-brain contrasts (ketamine vs placebo). Results are described at whole-brain level with cluster thresholds and anatomical localization. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study (3T) in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) inside the scanner. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME1+2) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and task contrasts (bias vs neutral cues; valid vs invalid stimuli) that relate directly to perceptual decision-making. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a recognized risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) during scanning, and it reports task-related contrasts and voxelwise group-level results. I4 satisfied: fMRI was acquired while participants performed a risky decision-making task. I5 satisfied: analyses include contrasts/metrics comparing risky versus safe decisions (risky–safe differential activation, group-by-decision effects). I6 satisfied: analyses were performed voxel-wise and a whole-brain analysis of group differences is reported (Supplementary Figure/Table), meeting the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map; I7 satisfied because whole-brain results are presented in the supplement and clearly described. The study is empirical (not a review), does not report only ROIs or connectivity, and includes full methods, results, and discussion in the provided full text, so no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that directly investigates risky decision-making using a child-friendly gambling paradigm (cake task). It includes task-related within-task contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; negative > positive feedback) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain results, tables of activations, and figures). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an ambiguity-laden perceptual/affective decision task (valence inferences on consonant vs dissonant musical intervals). The authors report group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses and relevant contrasts (e.g., intermediate dissonance > consonance, strong dissonance > intermediate) that map onto ambiguous decision-making comparisons (ambiguity > non-ambiguity). Whole-brain contrasts against baseline are reported with cluster-level FWE correction; the ambiguity-related contrasts were tested at the group voxelwise level and reported with small-volume correction for a priori ROIs (i.e., not ROI-only reporting). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (ambiguity-related within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E3 met: the fMRI second-level analyses were restricted to an a priori ROI mask (small-volume correction) rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a decision-making task manipulating probabilistic threat/risk), I5 (within-task contrasts across threat/risk levels and parametric effects), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables/text). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps reported; analyses were ROI-restricted). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Based on the ROI-restricted analysis, the study does not satisfy the whole-brain evidence requirement for inclusion in this meta-analysis, so it is excluded.

The article reports task-based fMRI in healthy human adults performing two-choice perceptual decision tasks (numerical and verbal) in the scanner (I4). It provides within-task contrasts (numerical task > baseline; verbal task > baseline) and task-related contrasts and practice effects (I5). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (full-factorial ANOVA, thresholded maps, and tables of coordinates) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Results are presented in figures and tables with coordinates (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a risky decision-making task (the Yellow Light Game) in the scanner. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Go > Stop decisions, Good > Bad outcomes, and outcome-by-decision parametric contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation analyses are reported (cluster-corrected via AFNI 3dClustSim) with tables and figures, and statistical maps uploaded to NeuroVault. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of a trust/reciprocity game (human subjects in scanner) and reports whole-brain, group-level SPM results (meets I4, I6, I7). However, the reported task contrasts focus on human vs. computer counterpart differences (e.g., human > computer) and conjunctions across cooperators vs noncooperators rather than contrasts that directly index risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, hard > easy). The manuscript does not present a within-task or between-task contrast explicitly relating to risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision-making as required by I5, so it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants who performed an odd–even-pass decision-making task with certain and uncertain (high-risk) conditions. The authors computed the contrast uncertain > certain at the single-subject level and carried out a random-effects, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (SPM8) with an uncorrected p<0.001 threshold and reported group activations and between-group comparisons in text, tables, and figures. The task and contrasts directly probe risky/ambiguous decision-making and the paper presents whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results (reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effects, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (phase 2 in scanner) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects, FWE cluster correction) with contrasts comparing perceptual/integration conditions (I:I, I:S, S:S). Coordinates and cluster statistics (MNI coords, cluster sizes, P values) are reported. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (coordinates/results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study implemented an fMRI probabilistic passive avoidance task in human participants making approach/avoid decisions under probabilistic outcomes (risk). The authors modeled expected value (EV) and prediction error (PE) and conducted first- and second-level (group) analyses. They report both ROI and whole-brain group-level (voxelwise) results (cluster-corrected whole-brain tables and figures), and describe contrasts corresponding to task-related decision-making (e.g., approached stimuli modulated by EV, avoided stimuli modulated by EV, punishment/reward feedback modulated by PE). Thus it satisfies: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making via EV/PE modulators), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used the weather prediction probabilistic category-learning task, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. Analyses were performed using an ROI-based SPM approach (AAL-derived masks) rather than an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map. Therefore the study violates the review requirements for (a) performing an eligible decision-making task (I4/I5) and (b) providing whole-brain task-evoked results (I6). It also meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI-based analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning task focused on feedback integration and reversal-related neural activity. While it is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level study (satisfying I6), the task does not clearly match the meta-analysis target domains of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the inclusion criteria. The reported contrasts (e.g., ALLNEG vs ALLPOS, FINREVERR vs REVERR, NEG+2 vs NEG+0, analysis of persistence after reversals) probe feedback- and reversal-related processes rather than explicit risk vs safe, uncertainty/ambiguity contrasts, or perceptual difficulty contrasts (I4 and I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (framing) task (meets I4). It includes within-task contrasts related to risk/framing (e.g., framing effect and reverse framing contrasts) and reports group-level contrasts (meets I5). Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM random-effects, with whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding; ROI SVC was applied but whole-brain results and coordinates are reported (meets I6 and I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and sufficient for screening. The study also reports PPI connectivity analyses but not as the sole output. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a lottery decision task involving estimation of reward probability (risky/uncertain decision making). The paper reports within-task, task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., regions correlating with posterior mean, prior mean, likelihood uncertainty, and interaction terms), corrected for multiple comparisons and reported with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Results are presented at the group level with whole-brain analyses and tables/figures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods (detailed fMRI acquisition and GLMs), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task, with participants scanned during task performance and a parametric (balloon-size/adjusted-pumps) within-task regressor. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (voxelwise correction, Monte Carlo simulations) and coordinates/activation maps are reported. The task and contrasts directly target risky decision-making, and whole-brain task-evoked effects are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for risky-DM fMRI whole-brain activation studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (categorical) decision-making task where choices are informed by accumulating probabilistic evidence. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM and ANOVA analyses (time series modeled over 16 time points), with corrected statistical maps (cluster-wise p < .05) and tables of ROIs with Talairach coordinates. Within-task contrasts/analyses directly probe decision-related processes (Rate of Evidence, evidence x time interactions, Rapid>Gradual>Switch and Switch>Gradual>Rapid patterns), satisfying the meta-analysis focus on perceptual/decision-making. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic reasoning (beads/JTC) task assessing decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguity). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguous decision-making (JTC task blocks vs control; last fish [decision] vs preceding fish), uses group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction, and reports peak coordinates (ROI results also provided). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study used an intertemporal delay-discounting task (choices between immediate vs. delayed rewards), which is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5. The paper does report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxel-wise GLM contrasts with cluster correction) and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (tables/supplement), so it meets I6 and I7. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., PumpsParametric > ControlParametric, PumpsAvg > ControlAvg, CashoutParametric, ExplosionParametric) (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with cluster correction (Z>2.3, p<0.05) and whole-brain results presented in tables and figures (meets I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes unmasked whole-brain task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is an empirical concurrent TMS-fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual detection task (signal detection at threshold), satisfying the review focus on perceptual decision-making. The paper reports within-task contrasts (hits, misses, correct rejections; e.g., misses > hits, misses > CR) and state-dependent TMS interactions relevant to perceptual decision processes. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise with permutation-based cluster correction and reported as whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (modified Asian disease life-death framing tasks) during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing positive vs negative framing and large vs small group contexts (risk-related contrasts). Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholds, MNI coordinates, tables and figures). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an empirical fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (near-threshold pain detection: subjects indicated on each trial whether a stimulus was perceived as painful or non-painful), satisfying I4. The paper includes within-task contrasts (pain vs. no pain during anticipation and stimulation) and trial-wise classification analyses tied to perceptual decisions, satisfying I5. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mass-univariate SPM contrasts and whole-brain SVM weight maps with FWE correction) meeting I6, and whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/supplemental material, satisfying I7. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in healthy adults that collected task-evoked BOLD data while participants performed probabilistic (risky) and intertemporal decision-making (I4 satisfied). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing probabilistic versus intertemporal valuation (e.g., R>D and D>R) and related analyses (I5 satisfied). Group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses are described and thresholded (cluster-corrected) with whole-brain results and tables (Table S2/S3), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps (I6). Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures is present (I7 satisfied). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Supplementary descriptions; core article content appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans using the Modified Cups Task, a risky monetary decision-making paradigm (meets I4). It includes within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making and prior outcomes (e.g., decision after loss vs decision after win; feedback risk loss vs risk win) (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps with cluster correction and reported peak tables/figures (meets I6 and I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task effects, and is empirical).

The study is excluded because it does not provide the required group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (I6). It does meet I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task—the Cups Task), I5 (reports within-task contrasts such as risky>safe), and I7 (reports MNI coordinates for results). However, task activation results were analyzed and reported using an anterior insula ROI mask (ROI-masked, not an unmasked whole-brain task activation map). Although the paper includes whole-brain PPI (connectivity) results, there is no unmasked, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported, so exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI task analyses with no whole-brain task results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study in humans using a two-choice prediction task with manipulated error rates (20% reward, 50% uncertainty, 80% punishment), i.e., risky/ambiguous decision-making, concurrent with an aversive interoceptive manipulation. Task-related decision-phase contrasts and error-rate effects are analyzed and reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (tables of significant clusters with coordinates and corrected thresholds; whole-brain interaction effects such as Group x ER x Interoception are reported and illustrated). Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision task), I5 (within-task/between-task contrasts related to risk/uncertainty/punishment), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I7 (results clearly described in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and original empirical fMRI task activation data are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (object categorisation under high vs low visibility). The paper reports task-related within-subject contrasts (high vs low visibility; object vs noise) and decodes choice-related contrasts (hard/guessing vs easy/visible). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise searchlight decoding with group-level random-effects statistics and FWE-corrected clusters, and coordinates/results are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual/target-detection task that explicitly models ambiguity (distance from 50% decision boundary) and perceptual similarity, and tests BOLD responses to these predictors. Inclusion criteria met: (I4) event-related fMRI during an active perceptual/decision task; (I5) within-task contrasts/regressors directly related to ambiguity and perceptual difficulty (ambiguity and similarity regressors; contrasts showing ambiguity> and similarity> effects); (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (FDR-corrected whole-brain results are described); (I7) whole-brain results presented in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of ambiguous and perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky sequential decision-making task (modified sequential risk-taking / BART-like). The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulators related to risk, missed opportunities (fictive losses), and loss-related effects, and links BOLD signal to subsequent choice. Analyses are group-level random-effects voxelwise GLMs (SPM8) with whole-brain results reported using voxel coordinates and corrected thresholds; region-of-interest small-volume corrections are used but whole-brain maps/coordinates are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study used BOLD fMRI during an intertemporal (temporal discounting) monetary decision-making task, which is value-based (delay discounting) rather than one of the meta-analysis target domains (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Although the study reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and within-task contrasts (e.g., hard>control, hard>easy), the task does not operationalize risky or ambiguous choices, nor is it a perceptual decision-making task in the conventional sense. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that collected BOLD data while participants performed a probabilistic reasoning (Box Task) decision-making paradigm (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to decision-making under uncertainty/ambiguity (e.g., conclusion > draw, draw > conclusion, and 60:40 > 80:20 reflecting higher uncertainty) (I5). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM voxelwise maps and corrected whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables (I6, I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; it reports whole-brain activation maps, not only ROI or connectivity-only results, and thus does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that manipulated uncertainty (‘uncertain event’ vs ‘certain reward’) during an emotional anticipation task, so it meets I4 (fMRI during human task) and I5 (contains an ambiguity-related contrast: ‘uncertain’ > ‘certain’). However, all reported group statistics are restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction; the paper does not present or describe unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore it fails I6 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-focused results with no whole-brain task map). Accordingly the study must be excluded.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (BART) and a cognitive-control task. It includes within-task contrasts directly related to risk processing (e.g., Pumps > Control; Cash Outs > Baseline) and uses parametric modulators for reward/pumps. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (FSL FLAME) with cluster-based familywise correction and tables/figures listing coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI on risky decisions), I5 (risk-related within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain task maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation in humans using the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), reports within-task contrasts comparing high-risk versus low-risk deck selections, and performs group-level mixed-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholded statistical maps (figures and tables of clusters reported). Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risky > safe contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task effects). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans where participants performed the Risky-Gains task during scanning (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (risky vs. safe choices) and voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses (one-sample and paired t-tests, voxel-wise correlation analyses) with reported coordinates and figures/supplementary results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical with original fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=26) performing a value-based buying task with probabilistic ratings (uncertainty/risk/ambiguity present). The authors report within-task, task-evoked contrasts (parametric modulators for accumulated value and accumulated evidence) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLMs, full-factorial group analysis, FWE-corrected results; tables/figures provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain group-level fMRI results of a probabilistic reversal-learning task, which involves decision-making under probabilistic/uncertain reinforcement (ambiguous/risky decision processes). Relevant within-task contrasts (punished reversal errors vs rewarded correct responses) are reported and interpreted as reflecting processing of violated reinforcement expectations/uncertainty. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed (ANCOVA with IQ covariate) and results are whole-brain thresholded and cluster-corrected; peak coordinates and clusters are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Although participants are adolescents rather than adults, the inclusion criteria did not restrict age. Given these points, the article meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria E3–E6.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing risky decision-making tasks (preferential vs. judgment-based choices). It includes within-task and between-task contrasts/parametric effects related to risk (e.g., sensitivity to unidimensional and intradimensional differences; paired t-tests comparing tasks). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (SPM5 random-effects, cluster correction) with results reported in text and figures/tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult human participants that collected BOLD signals while subjects performed a risky decision-making task (modified Lane task), satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., risky > safe during choice; win > safe; loss > safe), satisfying I5. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are described (AFNI group maps, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures/tables, meeting I6 and I7. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a card gambling task manipulating risk and reward during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making (linear risk-choice modulation; high-risk wins > low-risk wins) and presents group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain 2nd-level SPM analyses with tables/coordinates and FWE-corrected cluster/voxel results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). The study is therefore eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

Although this is an fMRI study with a human reinforcement-learning (probabilistic selection) task and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (satisfying I4, I6, I7), it does not provide any within- or between-task contrasts that map onto risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (e.g., risk > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, or hard > easy). The reported contrasts focus on feedback-related signals (signed/unsigned prediction errors) and post-error slowing/post-feedback BOLD modulations rather than explicit risk or ambiguity contrasts or perceptual difficulty contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in healthy participants performing a monetary gambling task probing risky decision making. The paper reports within-task contrasts including a linear gambling risk contrast (high-risk > low-risk) and outcome contrasts, conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM8 analyses with voxelwise cluster statistics, FWE correction and MNI coordinates reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and presents whole-brain task activation maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a monetary task that parametrically manipulates reward probability (0–100%), constituting decision making under risk/uncertainty. The paper reports within-task contrasts modeling effects of reward probability during expectation and outcome phases (linear contrasts of probability and prediction error), and second-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported statistical maps and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that implements a perceptual two-alternative forced-choice decision-making task (speech vs. non-speech discrimination with blended stimuli of varying difficulty). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., Speech: speech vs. non-speech; Correctness: correct vs. incorrect; Time and difficulty/ambiguity around 50–50 stimuli; learning-related contrasts), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM12 with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures of activations. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (coordinates/tables and text descriptions). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans in which participants performed a perceptual/motor decision-making task (wrist posture selection based on visual object orientation). The authors report a group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise analysis that parametrically modeled manual bistability (a measure of decision ambiguity/difficulty) as a predictor of BOLD activity, with results presented in figures and tables (cluster-corrected t-maps and coordinates). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast related to decision ambiguity/bistability), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this study acquired fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (I4) and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with results reported in tables/figures (I6, I7), it does not provide any within-task contrasts that map onto the meta-analysis’ targeted decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky > safe, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, hard > easy). The reported results focus on between-group interactions (diagnosis × phase, diagnosis × phase × accuracy) rather than an unmasked, whole-brain task effect or risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts of interest. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group interactions reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. As a result, this paper is ineligible for the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (masked object recognition) with event-related responses tied to recognition time. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (main effect of time map; voxelwise ANOVAs), figures of whole-brain activation, and tables of ROI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Relevant contrasts and analyses relate directly to perceptual decision processes (TR-dependent, correct vs. incorrect, static vs. shuffle), providing within-task contrasts tied to perceptual decision-making. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables descriptions and appears complete for screening. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (dot-motion) task with experimenter-controlled stimulus duration. The paper reports within-task contrasts relating to perceptual difficulty (motion coherence) and duration (e.g., parametric effects, motion coherence × duration interaction) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM beta maps, group ICA spatial maps normalized to MNI space, and thresholded task main-effect maps). Results are reported as whole-brain spatial maps and ROI tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The study used fMRI during a decision-making (card prediction) task and reports an Uncertain > Certain contrast, with cluster coordinates in Table 2 (meeting I4, I5, and I7). However, the reported results are presented only as between-group (stimulant users > controls) voxelwise t-tests for the Uncertain–Certain contrast, and the paper does not provide an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect map (i.e., the main task effect/within-group Uncertain > Certain whole-brain map is not reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (unmasked/group-level within-task whole-brain map not provided). Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination near perceptual threshold). It includes within-task contrasts directly related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., HF > FH, FFhc > HHhc, comparisons of hard/ambiguous trials), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected clusters and coordinates) alongside ROI results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task) during BOLD fMRI (I4 satisfied). Relevant within-task contrasts are reported, including risk effect (Bad > Good choices) and heightened-risk contrasts comparing framed messages to control (e.g., risky > safe type contrasts) (I5 satisfied). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with family-wise error correction and coordinates (whole-brain maps/coordinates reported) (I6 and I7 satisfied). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain task activation results (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (n=23) performing a probability-learning task with explicit decisions to buy/pass gambles (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to risk/uncertainty (active decision phase > control; parametric modulation by stimulus probability; entropy/choice-entropy effects) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholds, MNI coordinates, and tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing the Risky-Gains Task (risky decision-making), with behavioral contrasts examining risky vs safe and outcomes (gains vs losses). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (LME) with cluster correction; results are reported as whole-brain clusters and coordinates in tables/figures. Thus it meets I4 (task-based fMRI in humans on risky decisions), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/gain levels and risky>safe comparisons), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (Social Analogue Risk Task) during fMRI, reporting within-task contrasts (cash-out parametric modulator tracking increasing risk) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates. All inclusion criteria are met (I4: fMRI during a risky decision-making task; I5: within-task contrasts related to risk (cash-out PM, regressions); I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; I7: whole-brain results reported with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (N=19) that examined ambiguity in a decision-making task. The task manipulated contextual ambiguity (ambiguous vs generalization contexts) while subjects made choices under fMRI. The authors used model-based parametric regressors (Shannon entropy as a trial-wise ambiguity measure) and tested fMRI correlates time-locked to choice and outcome. They report group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected activations) and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described and illustrated. Thus: I4 (fMRI during ambiguous decision-making) is satisfied; I5 (within-task/task-related contrasts related to ambiguity) is satisfied via the ambiguity (entropy) regressor and contrasts; I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps) is satisfied by the SPM whole-brain analyses with correction; I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures) is satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that implemented a decision-making task with ambiguous (uncertain) and certain conditions and acquired task fMRI (REST, NO-PASS, PASS runs). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts comparing Uncertain > Certain, group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (FWE-corrected maps and cluster thresholds), and tables/coordinates of activations. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I4 (task fMRI during ambiguous decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast ambiguous > certain), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I7 (coordinates and full map details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes primary task activation maps, empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Blackjack). The paper reports within-task contrasts that directly index risk (e.g., high-risk hits > low-risk hits; low-risk sits > high-risk sits) and conducts random-effects, voxelwise, group-level analyses with reported whole-brain results and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and preprocessing), results (voxelwise contrasts and tables of coordinates), and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restriction).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between sure wins and lotteries) while scanned, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses related to risk valuation (correlations with certainty equivalents, offer magnitude; comparisons of advice present vs absent and age-group effects), satisfying I5. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates, satisfying I6 and acceptable reporting per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state, and not non-empirical. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky monetary decision-making task (50/50 gambles) during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/loss (e.g., gain > loss; neural loss aversion), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with stereotaxic MNI coordinates and tables/figures. While ROI analyses were also performed, whole-brain task-evoked results are clearly reported. Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG/fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney face/guitar categorization vs scrambled), with EEG-informed fMRI GLM analyses. The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLM results and contrasts (e.g., object vs. scrambled; HF>LF; LF>HF), with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of significant clusters. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study does not meet the review’s key task-domain inclusion criteria. Although it includes task-based fMRI with group-level, whole-brain activation maps (I6 satisfied) and reports results in text/tables/figures (I7 satisfied), the experimental paradigm is a sequential two-step reinforcement-learning task designed to dissociate model-based and model-free control, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) is not met, and I5 (at least one contrast explicitly related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, e.g., “risky > safe” or “hard > easy”) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I4 and I5 are not satisfied, despite I6 and I7 being satisfied.

Exclusion: The study does not report task contrasts of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required. It used a probabilistic reversal learning task and analyzed reward prediction error (RPE) parametric modulation; no contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy are reported. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise RPE maps and coordinates are provided, and results are reported in text/tables (so I6 and I7 are satisfied). However, it fails I4 (fMRI of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one within-task or between-task contrast explicitly related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in 30 healthy adult subjects performing a sequential investment task (risky decision-making) during scanning. The paper reports within-task model-based contrasts (TD errors and Q-values) related to risk preferences and decision-making, with whole-brain, voxelwise results (SPM8; voxelwise p<.001, cluster-corrected p<.05) and peak coordinates.
