Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical study with original fMRI data in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, fMRI analysis, and appendices).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a decision-making dice game that manipulates and measures risk (self-risk) and uncertainty about outcomes. The paper reports within-task contrasts/parametric modulators related to self-risk and other-need (e.g., positive association with self-risk, negative association with other-need) and factorial conditions (HS_HO, HS_LO, NS_HO, NS_LO). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results are reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction; peak coordinates and tables are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study reports fMRI during moral-judgment tasks in typically developing children/adolescents and contrasts ambiguous moral situations versus routine moral situations, so I4 (fMRI during a decision task) and I5 (an ambiguous > routine within-task contrast) appear satisfied. However I cannot verify critical reporting requirements: whether group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are presented (I6) or whether whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplementary material in sufficient detail (I7). Because the full article (methods, results, and voxelwise maps/tables) is unavailable, inclusion cannot be confirmed. No explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E5, E6) are identifiable from the abstract alone. Therefore I exclude this record due to incomplete full text preventing verification of I6/I7 and overall eligibility.

This paper reports a methods development and validation study (Hidden Process Models) using an fMRI sentence–picture verification task. It does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or canonical perceptual decision-making as defined for this review. Specifically: (a) I4 not met — the task is semantic/verification (sentence vs picture) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making; (b) I5 not met — no within-task contrasts of the form relevant to the review (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, risk>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity) are reported; (c) I6 not met — although voxelwise SPM maps are shown for example participants, the paper does not present group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for decision-making contrasts of interest. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (2IFC Gabor orientation detection), so inclusion criterion I4 is satisfied. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or conventional within-task/between-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., hard>easy, task>baseline). Analyses are ROI-based multivoxel decoding and pre/post spontaneous activity comparisons confined to retinotopic and anatomical ROIs. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. Because the report presents only ROI-based analyses without whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E3 applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study manipulating outcome ambiguity (ambiguous outcome group vs differential outcome group) during a task in which subjects executed stimulus–response instructions and received ambiguous or differential outcomes. The paper reports whole-brain first-level GLMs (late vs early practice contrasts per subject), a group-level whole-brain two-sample t-test (univariate; reported as null after correction), and whole-brain multivariate classification/weight maps with peak coordinates and tables. The between-group contrast directly pertains to ambiguity (AOG vs DOG), and whole-brain voxelwise maps/coordinates are provided (main text and supplementary), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed a prediction task during scanning (a perceptual decision task about which symbol would appear next). The paper reports within-task contrasts (structured vs. random sequences; pre vs. post training) tied to the decision/prediction task, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster-corrected statistical maps described in the text and shown in figures. Whole-brain results are reported (GLM maps, voxelwise analyses), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making and should be included.

This study used fMRI during the Ultimatum Game, a social fairness-based decision-making task, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and presents whole-brain results in text/tables (meets I6 and I7). However it does not meet I4 (task type: not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and I5 (no within-task contrasts defined as risky vs safe, ambiguity contrasts, or perceptual difficulty contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a visual perceptual decision-making (categorization) task while ignoring congruent/incongruent auditory input. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects), providing coordinates and cluster-level inferences for contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., incongruent > congruent; interactions with visual/auditory reliability; degraded > intact visual; reaction-time–related activity). Dynamic causal modeling is also reported but does not replace the whole-brain activation results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies are satisfied (I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI study in humans performing a decision-making task (two-choice prediction) manipulating error/uncertainty rates (20%, 50%, 80%) and includes within-task contrasts (planned 20% vs 80% error-rate). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were conducted (AFNI processing, cluster-correction) with results reported as activation clusters/coordinates (tables and figures). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports a whole-brain fMRI study of human participants performing a Communication Game involving asymmetric information and choices to give true vs false advice. It includes group-level whole-brain activation maps (LME) and ROI analyses, and thus meets I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task involving uncertainty/social risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). However, it does not provide any within-task or between-task contrast explicitly targeting risky vs safe, high-risk vs low-risk, ambiguity vs non-ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty contrasts as required by I5. The primary task contrast is true advice > false advice (social/honesty decision), and reported effects of risk propensity are correlational (trait RTI effects), rather than a task-evoked “risk > safe” type contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are violated. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that acquired task-based BOLD during the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts (e.g., Inflate*p(Explode), Success*p(Explode), Explode*p(Explode)), which index risk- and reward-related modulation, satisfying the requirement for at least one within-task contrast related to risky decision-making. Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise inference (whole-brain search space, cluster correction) and results are reported in tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this study acquired group-level, whole-brain fMRI data and reports voxelwise task-evoked maps (satisfying I6 and I7), the experimental paradigm is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task focusing on reward prediction errors and approach/avoidance learning. The paper does not present any within-task or between-task contrasts that map onto the meta-analysis domains of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., high- vs low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or hard > easy perceptual difficulty) at the whole-brain level. Behavioral analyses concern approach vs avoidance and win–win/lose–lose performance, but no corresponding whole-brain contrasts of risk/ambiguity or choice difficulty are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s domain-specific inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I6 — the paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked fMRI results (SPM8 second-level analyses with reported peak coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — although fMRI was acquired during a probabilistic reward learning/confirmation task, the task is an associative probabilistic reward-learning paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined for the meta-analysis; and I5 — the paper does not report any within- or between-task contrasts framed as risky vs safe, high- vs low-risk, ambiguity vs non-ambiguity, or hard vs easy perceptual contrasts (primary contrasts are emotion: fearful vs neutral, and model-based RPE regressors). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports ROI and decoding analyses confined to early visual areas (V1–V3) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (within-task analyses relating neural signals to perceptual decision variables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study uses an fMRI value-based decision-making task (BDM auction) comparing food vs nonfood valuation after sleep deprivation. It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports peak coordinates (meets I6 and I7). However, it does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks or contrasts (does not meet I4 or I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain task-evoked analyses (PCLT > control) and reports voxelwise group results; however, the experimental task is a probabilistic category learning task (probabilistic feedback/category learning), which is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no contrast that is meaningfully related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to risk (decision > no-decision; risky > safe; wins > losses) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM2) with family-wise error correction for the main task effect and tables/figures of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making paradigm (modified Iowa Gambling Task), satisfying I4. fMRI contrasts and analyses relate neural activity during decision-making to risk-avoidance behavior (decision>fixation and mediation of VST/RDLPFC activity), meeting I5. The paper performs voxelwise, whole-brain mediation analyses (MEPM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise mediator maps and results in figures/tables, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; it is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects rather than only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that directly manipulates ambiguity in decision-making (external subjective decision, ESD) and contrasts ambiguous versus veridical conditions (ESD > EVD). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses are reported with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates. The report includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during ambiguous decision task), I5 (ambiguous > non-ambiguous contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling task that manipulates risk levels (risky decision-making), reporting within-task contrasts (high-risk vs low-risk outcomes, positive vs negative outcomes) and group-by-risk interactions. The analysis uses whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses with reported stereotactic coordinates and FWE-corrected cluster peaks (tables and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI during an intertemporal delay-discounting (monetary) task rather than a risky-, ambiguous-, or perceptual-decision-making task as defined by the review. Although the authors report a group-level whole-brain Hard > Easy contrast (figure and whole-brain analysis) meeting I6 and I7, the task does not probe risk or ambiguity, nor is it a perceptual decision-making paradigm (so I4 and I5 are not satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: the paper reports whole-brain task activation (not ROI-only), and is an empirical fMRI study with group-level maps. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making) during scanning, reporting contrasts of high-risk versus low-risk choices. The authors conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3×2×3 ANOVA covarying for age) and report whole-brain interaction activations (voxel-wise thresholding with cluster-level AlphaSim correction) with results in tables/figures. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext is complete.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a prediction/statistical-learning task (learning frequency and context-based sequences). It does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (no risk vs safe, ambiguity contrasts, or perceptual difficulty/coherence contrasts). There are no task contrasts reported that match the meta-analysis inclusion (e.g., “risky>safe”, “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”); analyses focus on ICA components, component β changes, and functional network connectivity correlated with strategy, not on group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts for risky/ambiguous/perceptual-DM. Full text appears complete. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 (and does not provide the required whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise contrasts per I6). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are strictly met. Excluded on the basis of not meeting inclusion criteria.

The study reports event-related fMRI in human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (decision-making under risk/uncertainty), includes within-task contrasts defined as risk effects (bad deck > good deck) and heightened-risk effects across message frames, and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR-corrected results and reported MNI coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of contrasts and whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic loss-learning (reinforcement learning) task (meets I4). However, the neuroimaging analyses were masked to the striatum (ROI-focused) and do not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map, so the study fails the whole-brain requirement (I6) and does not provide the typical within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (I5). This violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (mixed monetary gambles) and performed within-task parametric contrasts (e.g., EV, kLOSE), so I4 and I5 are satisfied. However, the paper reports ROI-based univariate analyses and ROI-based effective connectivity (PPI, DCM) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it fails I6 and meets exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports effective connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it acquired whole-brain fMRI while participants performed a two-choice gambling task (risky decision-making) and reports within-task contrasts related to risk (risk-magnitude parametric regressors and risk-related activations). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8, FWE-corrected results, tables and figures), and results are presented in tables/figures/supplementary material. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps, and is empirical).

This empirical fMRI study scanned healthy human participants (n=30 in fMRI sample) while they performed a binary trust task that contrasts trusting (risky) versus not trusting (safe) decisions and human-versus-computer conditions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) are reported with coordinates and FWE results for contrasts such as trusting > not trusting and human > computer, and interaction effects; results are presented as whole-brain activations (tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, task, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, GLM), Results, and Discussion. Thus the study addresses risky decision-making, includes task-related contrasts, and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task—an uncertainty-based decision-making paradigm relevant to ambiguous decision-making. The study reports within-task contrasts related to reinforcement/uncertainty (positive prediction error, positive vs. negative prediction errors, task-related BOLD responses, and behaviorally-relevant contrasts) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxelwise thresholds, cluster-correction, whole-brain maps used as functional masks, and whole-brain group contrasts). Results and contrasts are clearly described in the text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task activation, not between-group-only without an unmasked task effect, and not non-empirical). Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans that administered perceptual decision-making tasks (nonsymbolic numerosity comparison and a brightness control), meeting the review’s perceptual-DM domain. The paper reports within-task contrasts relating difficulty/congruity (e.g., parametric/‘hard>easy’-like effects and task×difficulty interaction) and directly tests activity modulated by difficulty/congruity levels. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (ANOVA and parametric GLM), with cluster-corrected results and reported coordinates/figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Meets inclusion criteria: fMRI was performed while participants completed a decision-making task (probabilistic 'weather prediction' classification), and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to uncertainty/predictive value (e.g., high > low predictive value) and task vs control contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise models with FDR correction; results are reported as Talairach coordinates and cluster tables. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Therefore the study is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study uses a probabilistic reinforcement learning task in participants with autism and reports whole-brain voxelwise activation maps. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required. Specifically, there are no within-task or between-task contrasts directly comparing risk levels, ambiguity/uncertainty conditions, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., “high risk > low risk”, “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”, or “hard > easy”). The reported contrasts focus on stimulus vs feedback epochs, early vs late learning, win-stay/lose-shift behavior, and parametric modulators of learning probability, which reflect reinforcement learning processes rather than explicit risk/ambiguity or perceptual decision contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are met (whole-brain, clearly reported results), but I4 and I5 are not met (task/contrasts are not of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study used fMRI during an ultimatum game (social economic decision-making) and reports whole-brain, cross-subject multivariate classification results with reported MNI coordinates. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review objective. Although within-task contrasts (accepted vs. rejected; high vs. low offers) are reported, these contrasts are not framed as or directly related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. Therefore it fails to meet I4 (task type) and I5 (contrast relevance). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task. The authors report within-task, parametrically modulated contrasts related to risk (e.g., InflationChoice * P(explode), SuccessfulInflation * P(explode)). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported with cluster-level thresholds and FWE-corrected peak coordinates (tables and figures provided). Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) an fMRI risky decision task, (I5) at least one within-task contrast related to risk, (I6) a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map, and (I7) acceptable reporting of whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include whole-brain task effects, and are empirical). The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study collected fMRI in healthy human participants performing a category-learning (decision) task and used model-based regressors indexing uncertainty (entropy) and item contrasts (exceptions vs rule-following), so it meets I4 (task fMRI in humans) and I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/ambiguity). However, all neuroimaging analyses were high-resolution region-of-interest (MTL and striatum) ROI-based group analyses; the paper does not report an unmasked, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level task activation map. Therefore it fails I6 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion rationale: no qualifying whole-brain/group voxelwise task maps (E3), despite meeting I4 and I5; thus excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual categorization/decision task (information-integration A/B categorization). The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric contrasts related to perceptual decision difficulty/uncertainty (e.g., comparisons of Near-bound vs Far, parametric distance-from-bound and distance-from-prototype), which map onto perceptual decision-making contrasts (hard>easy analogues). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study includes contrasts of ambiguous (surprised) vs neutral faces and reports group-level whole-brain analyses, it does not meet the requirement that participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task during scanning. The valence ratings (decision task) were collected in a prior behavioral session outside the scanner; during the fMRI face runs participants 'freely viewed' faces rather than making in-scanner valence decisions. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (fMRI during an explicit decision-making task) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (ambiguous > non-ambiguous contrast [Surprise > Neutral]), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an audio-visual associative learning task that required explicit trial-by-trial predictions about visual outcomes. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLMs) and presents whole-brain FWE-corrected activations for parametric contrasts tied to computational quantities reflecting perceptual outcome PEs and higher-level uncertainty/volatility (ε2, ε3, ψ2, ψ3, μ3, ε_ch). These regressors index perceptual decision processes and uncertainty/ambiguity (precision-weighted PEs and volatility), which map onto the review’s perceptual and ambiguous decision-making contrasts (e.g., high vs. low uncertainty). Results are reported at the whole-brain level (and in ROI masks), replicated across two fMRI samples, and described in the main text with supplemental materials available. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual sequence-detection task with decision responses (button press/release). It includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual/ambiguity decision-making (e.g., CHECK_HIGH > CHECK_LOW, TERM > EXT, surprise parametric effects) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and coordinate tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all review inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a human fMRI study in healthy adults using an event-related paradigm manipulating reward probability and magnitude (slot-machine task) that targets risk/uncertainty processing. It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk/uncertainty (e.g., Delay: Slot_B > Slot_A for reward uncertainty; S1 Slot_B > Slot_A; S2 contrasts comparing probabilities). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects SPM99 results with tables and figures (whole-brain coordinates reported). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents performing an economic lottery task that manipulates risk (coefficient of variation) during scanning, satisfying I4. The authors modeled a within-task parametric contrast of risk (CV of chosen gambles) and report group-level GLM whole-brain results, satisfying I5 and I6 (cluster-level FWE-corrected whole-brain analyses and peak coordinates provided). Whole-brain results are described and peak coordinates are reported in text/appendices, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 4) in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (accept/reject lotteries), meeting I4. It reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulators directly related to risk (variance) and valence (e.g., variance correlation, gain > loss, accept > reject, and interactions), meeting I5. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLMs with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of activations provided, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including fMRI acquisition and GLM), Results (whole-brain corrected activations, tables), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical fMRI study in healthy adults). Thus the study should be included.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (framing task: sure vs. gamble), with relevant within-task contrasts (e.g., framing effect: (Gsure+Lgamble) − (Ggamble+Lsure)) and additional contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (cluster-based correction and whole-brain regression results; tables of coordinates and figures are provided), and ROI/SVC analyses are supplementary to whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) during scanning in 10–14-year-old participants. It reports within-task contrasts (Choose Inflate vs Choose Win; Outcome Inflate vs Outcome Explode; parametric modulation of explosion probability) that relate directly to risky decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (AFNI GLM, cluster-wise correction) with results reported in tables and figures. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of the above. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic two-step decision-making task with monetary outcomes (i.e., decisions under known probabilistic uncertainty). The authors report within-task parametric contrasts linking decision-related computational variables (state prediction errors and reward prediction errors) to BOLD signal during decision and outcome states, and they conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and report coordinates. Thus the study meets the review’s requirement for an fMRI task involving risky/uncertain decision-making, includes appropriate within-task contrasts related to decision-making, and provides whole-brain group-level statistical maps (coordinates and figures). It does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical design).

This study collected fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (I4 satisfied). However, the reported neuroimaging analyses are ICA-based component maps and component-level regressions (beta weights) relating component time courses to task regressors; the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrast map (e.g., task>fixation or hard>easy) suitable for coordinate-based inclusion. Thus it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports ICA/task-related connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear voxelwise within-task/between-task contrast maps reported in the paper), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Exclusion based on scope and analysis type. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (reports ROI-focused task analyses without presenting an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI task is passive viewing of food images, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making; reported contrast is fattening > non-fattening food), I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map reported; analyses focused on predefined ROIs). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is excluded.

Full text reports an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (satisfies I6) and results/tables/figures are clearly described (satisfies I7). However, the experimental paradigm is probabilistic reversal learning, not a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The reported contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses; nonswitch errors vs correct responses) are not contrasts of risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) and therefore do not meet I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis domain-specific inclusion criteria (I4, I5).

This fMRI study involved human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (forced-choice categorization of ambiguous /a?a/ stimuli as /aba/ vs /ada/) during scanning, satisfying I4. It includes task-related contrasts (auditory post-test trials > baseline) and trial-level analyses tied to perceptual responses (perceptual-label GLM and multivariate decoding distinguishing /aba/ vs /ada/), satisfying I5. Group-level whole-brain GLM contrasts are reported and corrected for multiple comparisons and visualized on cortical surfaces (whole-brain task-evoked maps), satisfying I6. Results are presented as whole-brain maps and described in the text/figures, consistent with I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses of the habenula and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Exclusion(s) met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion(s) met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic/risky decision-making task with monetary gains/losses), I5 (within-task contrasts relevant to decision-making, e.g., loss > win and high vs low loss-probability contrasts). Inclusion(s) not met: I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported), and therefore I7 (not applicable because whole-brain results are not provided). Additional notes: analyses focus on manually segmented habenula ROIs (and a nearby thalamic control region); the paper does not present unmasked whole-brain statistical maps or coordinate tables for task activation, and scanning was targeted to slices centered on the epithalamus, further indicating lack of whole-brain coverage. Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reported relevant contrasts (e.g., high-risk [25%] vs low-risk [75%]), satisfying I4 and I5. However, all reported statistical results are ROI-based (voxel-wise tests within a priori prefrontal masks with small-volume correction); no unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or whole-brain results are presented in the manuscript. Therefore it fails I6 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain map). Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study with human participants performing decision-making tasks (prisoner’s dilemma and stag hunt) that manipulate risk/uncertainty in social decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts (PD > SH) examining differences in cognitive demands and neural activation, provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with multiple-comparison correction, and reports coordinates/tables of significant clusters. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly addresses perceptual decision-making: participants made forced-choice phoneme categorizations of ambiguous sounds (perceptual decisions) after audiovisual exposure. Inclusion criteria met: I4 — fMRI collected while participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (auditory post-tests/phoneme categorization); I5 — within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making were reported (behaviorally weighted contrast linking exposure-block activation to subsequent perceptual choices; audiovisual blocks vs baseline and GLMs modeling auditory post-tests); I6 — group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (cortex-based aligned group GLMs with cluster-size correction); I7 — whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables with peak coordinates and stats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext appears complete.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing the Salience Attribution Test, a probabilistic reward-learning task involving high- vs low-probability cue contrasts (adaptive reward prediction) and comparisons of cues associated with identical (50%) probabilities (ambiguity/aberrant reward prediction). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM5), with whole-brain FWE correction and coordinates reported; results include voxelwise and cluster-level maps and small-volume corrections. Thus the paper includes an fMRI decision-making task (I4), within-task contrasts relevant to risk/uncertainty/ambiguity (I5), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I6) with coordinates described in text/tables (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in human adolescent females making decisions about stimuli labeled as high- vs low-risk (sexual decisions with high/low risk descriptors, plus control food/item conditions), satisfying the requirement of an fMRI scan during risky decision-making (I4). The paper includes explicit within-task contrasts of risk (high-risk > low-risk and beta-based group contrasts; e.g., Boys (High-risk − Low-risk) vs. (Food + Item)) fulfilling I5. Analyses were performed at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise preprocessing and statistical mapping (spatial normalization to Talairach, voxelwise thresholds, cluster extent via Monte Carlo simulation) and significant clusters are reported in tables/figures, meeting I6 and I7. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that acquired whole-brain functional MRI while participants performed a two-round Trust Game that required monetary decision-making under social uncertainty/risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Fair – Control; Unfair – Control) that compare the decision-making task to a control cursor-adjustment task, meeting the requirement for an experimental task > control contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 with reported thresholds and cluster/FWE corrections, and results are reported in tables and figures. Thus the study satisfies I4 (fMRI during decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts relevant to decision-making: task>control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in adolescents using the Stoplight driving task (risky decision-making) during BOLD fMRI. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risky decisions (Go > Stop; Stop > Go; Crash vs No-Crash) at the group level, using whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates, cluster thresholds, and tables/figures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task, contrasts, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (BART), so I4 is met. However, the paper reports ROI-based, model-driven effective connectivity (GIMME) analyses and person-/group-level directed networks rather than group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or standard within-task voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it does not meet I5 (no reported within-task/between-task voxelwise contrasts for risk) nor I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map as the target analysis). Exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (effective/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) are therefore triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it fails to provide the required whole-brain task-evoked statistical map or voxelwise contrasts (I5, I6 not met); E3 and E4 apply, while I4 is satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=24) who performed risky decision-making (Self trials) while being scanned, meeting I4. The paper reports within-task voxelwise contrasts relating neural activity to trial-by-trial risk at the time of decision (parametric risk regressor; caudate activity), satisfying I5. Results are reported as group-level whole-brain analyses with FWE-corrected clusters and referenced tables/figures, fulfilling I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activations; not connectivity-only; not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is an fMRI study of a risky decision-making task (game of Chicken) and includes analyses of risky versus safe choices, the paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical map specifically for a risky>safe (or equivalent) contrast. The reported whole-brain results pertain to the human-versus-computer (counterpart) effect; selection (risky vs safe) effects are described only via parameter estimates at peak voxels derived from the counterpart map (i.e., not presented as an independent whole-brain contrast). Meta-analysis inclusion requires a task-related, group-level, whole-brain activation map for the risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast. Therefore I4 and I5 are met, but I6 is not met (no whole-brain voxelwise risky-related map reported). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during an intertemporal (delay discounting) monetary decision-making task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task required by the review. No contrasts explicitly index risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy perceptual coherence) and the reported analyses focus on ROI-based valuation and cognitive-control regions using small-volume corrections rather than providing an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map. Therefore it fails the inclusion criteria requiring (I4) a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task, (I5) task contrasts related to those DM domains, and (I6) whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results. It meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports ROI-focused analyses without whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5, I6.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports task-evoked fMRI during a pilot landing-decision task (I4 satisfied) and reports within-task contrasts/conditions (e.g., decision vs control; correct vs incorrect) (I5 satisfied). However, the manuscript presents results based on ROI-based analyses (bilateral caudate and other ROIs) using small-volume correction and reports extracted ROI activation values; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps, tables of whole-brain coordinates, or whole-brain figures are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and does not satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study is an fMRI pain-conditioning experiment examining predictability-mediated pain modulation and does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (inclusion criteria I4 not met). Although it contrasts uncertain vs. certain contexts (S2U>S2C), these are pain-predictability/pain-rating contrasts rather than within-task or between-task contrasts of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I5 not met). The paper does provide group-level whole-brain task activation results (I6) and reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task that manipulated reward probabilities (HP 90% vs LP 75%), i.e., decision-making under uncertainty (risky/ambiguous context). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to decision uncertainty (e.g., reversal errors vs positive feedback, NEG+1 vs NEG+0, prediction-error-related regressors) and condition comparisons (HP vs LP). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (FSL, reported coordinates and whole-brain results). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study administered a probability discounting (risky decision-making) task during scanning (meets I4) and reports task-related comparisons (probability vs certain) via component beta weights (meets I5). However, the analysis uses independent component analysis (ICA) to identify task-related networks and reports component spatial maps and beta weights rather than a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical activation map. No unthresholded or voxelwise GLM task activation maps or coordinate-based whole-brain task results are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ICA/task-related network analyses without whole-brain task activation maps) and does not meet I6. Full text appears complete. Inclusion_criteria_met: I4, I5. Inclusion_criteria_not_met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic decision-making task (Paper-Scissors-Rock) that involves learning and executing risky/uncertain reward contingencies. The authors report within-task contrasts separating early (learning/uncertain) versus late (established/probabilistic) decision trials and group-by-decision-time interaction effects, directly relating to risky/ambiguous decision-making. Analyses were performed as group-level, voxelwise whole-brain linear mixed effects with multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim), and results are reported in text and figures (supplementary tables referenced). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and whole-brain task activation maps are reported).

The study acquired 3T fMRI while participants performed social and non-social two-arm bandit tasks that manipulated probabilistic reward structures and volatility (uncertainty), which constitute decision-making under risk/ambiguity. The authors implemented whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with amplitude-modulated regressors for value expectation, prediction error, and volatility (uncertainty), and reported group-level whole-brain results (tables of coordinates, figures, and corrected cluster-wise inference; see Table 2 and figures). These analyses provide within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/ambiguous decision-making (via the volatility regressor) and other decision-related computations. The paper is an empirical fMRI study with whole-brain task activation maps reported, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary material). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using a decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) performed during BOLD fMRI (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risky decision making (high vs. moderate risk/reward; high vs. equal; moderate vs. equal) during the selection phase (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain linear regressions, cluster-corrected maps and table/figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6, I7). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This article reports an empirical fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) in human participants who performed an on-task decision paradigm (number magnitude selections), meeting the requirement for a task-evoked fMRI scan (I4). The study presents within-task contrasts related to decision difficulty/conflict (e.g., incongruent > non-switch control; congruent > switch control), which map onto perceptual/decision-making contrasts (analogous to hard > easy or task > control), satisfying I5. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, random-effects voxelwise maps with reported thresholding and tables of coordinates (I6), and results are reported in tables/figures within the text (I7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study includes an fMRI experiment (N=19) in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (face emotion judgments under varying ambiguity). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguity (e.g., increasing ambiguity >, decreasing ambiguity >), and describes voxelwise, group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (SPM8, second-level random-effects) with reported activations and thresholding; results are presented in figures and Supplementary Table 1. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during decision task), I5 (ambiguity-related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human males performing a Stag-hunt task, which is a risky, mutually beneficial decision-making paradigm. It includes a within-task contrast (Stag > Rabbit) directly related to risky decision-making, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (two-sample t-tests) with reported coordinates and tables (left dlPFC cluster). Whole-brain functional connectivity analyses are also reported, but whole-brain activation results for the task contrast are present, not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans using a gambling-like probabilistic reversal learning task with monetary outcomes (decision-making under probabilistic risk). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected, tables and figures), and relevant contrasts are provided including reward > punishment and final reversal error (behavioural switching) > baseline, which reflect task-evoked processes related to risky decision-making and feedback-guided choice. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Although many contrasts focus on feedback, the paradigm and the ‘behavioural switching’ contrast capture decision-related processes under uncertainty, meeting the review’s scope. Minor caveat: contrasts are more feedback-focused than explicit ‘risky > safe’ contrasts, but inclusion criteria allow experimental task > control and related within-task contrasts. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

Study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sexual risk: high vs low) with behavioral ratings. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing low vs high risk (and correlations with behavior), and a random-effects, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM (thresholded and reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task involving risky choices and brief perceptual discriminations (vowel vs consonant). The study acquired task-based whole-brain BOLD data at the group (random-effects) level, ran voxelwise GLM analyses, and reported whole-brain activations with coordinates (insula, striatum, IPS, lOFC) and statistical thresholds; it also conducted PPI connectivity but did not rely solely on ROI/connectivity results. Relevant within-task contrasts (e.g., choice onset and successful perceptual trials: Discouragement > Control; hard/difficult trials at P=0.6) directly index risky and perceptual decision-making. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports a human fMRI experiment in which participants performed a risky decision-making (certainty-equivalent) task during BOLD acquisition (meets I4). The paper presents within-task contrasts directly relevant to risk (low-probability vs high-probability prospects and high-value vs low-value prospects) (meets I5). Analyses are voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain AFNI analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates (meets I6 and I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (N=82) who performed a probabilistic binary lottery decision-making task with monetary incentives and varying cue probabilities (explicit probabilities such as 75:25, 55:45), i.e., decisions under risk. The authors modelled task-related decision variables (e.g., adviser fidelity during the decision phase, precision-weighted prediction errors at outcome) and used these as parametric modulators in a voxelwise, group-level GLM. They report whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected peaks and clusters with MNI coordinates) and ROI analyses, with conjunctions across two samples. Thus inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulators related to decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (clearly reported whole-brain results/coordinates) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under probabilistic reward), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts using a computational model-derived prediction error parametric modulator and reports RPE-related activation (i.e., task-evoked, decision-related contrasts), satisfying I5. Analyses were conducted as group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses with reported voxelwise results and correction procedures; VBM and whole-brain RPE networks are described, satisfying I6. Whole-brain results and peak coordinates/tables/figures are reported in the text and tables, satisfying I7. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (N=30) who performed a choice reaction-time task manipulating uncertainty/entropy (response alternatives and reversal). The study reports within-task contrasts that index uncertainty/perceptual difficulty (linear entropy contrasts, reversal > nonreversal, etc.), conducts first- and second-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses and multilevel mediation, and presents group-level whole-brain statistical maps and results. These meet inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-like/perceptual task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty/perceptual difficulty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I7 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task maps, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain task analyses (meets I6) and reports whole-brain results in text/figures (meets I7), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. The task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning paradigm with reward prediction error (RPE) parametric contrasts and emotional-bias (emotional > neutral) contrasts, but the paper does not present any within-task or between-task contrasts explicitly mapping risky vs safe, high- vs low-risk, ambiguity vs non-ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (does not meet I4 or I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision-making meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that explicitly manipulates and analyzes reward uncertainty (variance) and expected value. Participants performed an in-scanner task involving stimuli with varying reward magnitudes and probabilities (risk manipulation); voxelwise, group-level SPM2 random-effects analyses and regressions were reported with MNI coordinates and thresholding (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked maps). Within-task contrasts/regressions directly related to uncertainty (inverted-U variance function) and value were tested and reported. The paper is complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants who performed a decision-making task involving risky and neutral choices (Social Context Decision Task). It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risky decision-making and outcome valence (e.g., Regret > Disappointment, Regret > Relief, Relief > Elation, Disappointment > Elation, Negative > Positive), which map onto risky vs non-risky and negative vs positive outcome contrasts. Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM8 procedures and report cluster coordinates and statistical thresholds. Thus the paper meets I4 (task fMRI during risky decisions), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/cluster tables). It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making task (face-based gender/affect judgments), satisfying the review scope (perceptual decision-making). The experiment includes within-task contrasts and task-evoked analyses (e.g., univariate GLM contrasts such as switch > stay, trial-wise decoding metrics) conducted on task data. The methods describe voxelwise GLM processing and group-level statistical testing, and results/figures report task-related activation and decoding at the group level, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (reported in text/figures). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults that manipulated perceptual decision uncertainty (dot-pattern prototype distortion) and measured brain activity during task performance. It includes contrasts directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (parametric modulation of uncertainty/hard > easy and training-related contrasts) and feedback valence contrasts. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise, and results are reported with whole-brain FDR-corrected maps and tables/figures. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during reward processing (Monetary Incentive Delay and a probabilistic reward-learning task) in depressed and control participants, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making), and I6 (main reported imaging analyses are ROI-based; no clear group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for a decision-making contrast is presented). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are specifically triggered beyond the primary mismatch with the review topic. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain analyses (coordinates reported) but the behavioral task is an implicit serial reaction time (SRT) dual task designed to probe implicit sequence learning and response conflict. The study does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (e.g., risky vs safe, ambiguity/uncertainty contrasts, or perceptual difficulty/coherence contrasts). Thus it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (task must be a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). It does satisfy I6 (group-level whole-brain task activation reported) and I7 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the article is excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It acquired functional MRI while healthy adult participants performed a risky decision-making task (Trust Game) (I4). The authors report task-related contrasts (GAME > CONTROL; INVESTOR > CONTROL; TRUSTEE > CONTROL), i.e., experimental task > control contrasts relevant to risk-based decision-making (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (two-sample t-tests, voxelwise p<0.001 uncorrected) and results are reported with tables of coordinates and figures (I6,I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not appear truncated. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group without whole-brain task maps). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task activation results from a behavioral decision-making task (probabilistic reversal learning), it does not report contrasts that map onto the meta-analysis' target domains of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., contrasts such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts focus on feedback valence and behavioral responses (lose-stay vs. win-stay, lose-shift vs. lose-stay, valence and shift-related contrasts) within a reinforcement-learning/set-shifting paradigm rather than explicit risk/ambiguity or perceptual-difficulty contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, and per screening rules the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a behavioral decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task analyses), I7 (whole-brain results reported and described). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-task or between-task contrast specifically related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study (n=26) in which participants performed a risky monetary decision-making task (choices between certain and gamble options) while BOLD data were acquired. The authors report group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses with reported coordinates and corrected statistics (voxel-wise threshold P<0.001; cluster-level small-volume correction), and regressions/parametric contrasts relating task variables (EV, RPE, chosen certain rewards) to BOLD activity in ventral striatum and insula. Results are described with coordinates and figures/tables. Thus the study includes (I4) fMRI during risky decision-making, (I5) within-task parametric contrasts related to risk/values, (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses, and (I7) reporting of results via coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a wheel-of-fortune gambling task (50% chance) involving decisions to play for rewards (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk/reward (e.g., anticipation for reward trials > non-reward control; outcome won vs not won; magnitude-dependent contrasts) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of coordinates and reported clusters. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (Experiment 3) employing a lottery task that manipulates outcome uncertainty and expected value. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction and provide tables/figures of coordinates and contrasts. They report parametric modulation of neural activity by outcome uncertainty (i.e., increasing OU) during curiosity induction (analogous to a high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty contrast) and contrasts for outcome presentation (Curiosity Relief–Yes > Curiosity Relief–No). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLM), Results, and Discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study with task-evoked activation maps (meets I6) and reports whole-brain results/coordinates (meets I7), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required. The task is an olfactory intensity evaluation combined with a memory (cognitive load) manipulation; the reported contrasts are odor > no-odor and cognitive-load effects/interactions, not perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence) or risky/ambiguous decision contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one within- or between-task contrast explicitly related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports fMRI during a two-step sequential decision-making task and analyses model-based vs model-free signals; however it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses reported with FWE-corrected peaks and coordinates) and I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI while performing a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one within-task or between-task contrast related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 and E5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. This fMRI study acquired task data during a decision-making (number-guessing reward) task and reports relevant contrasts (Win-Control, Loss-Control), satisfying I4 and I5. However, all group-level statistical analyses were conducted and thresholded within an a priori reward-circuitry ROI mask (Z-statistic images were thresholded in the reward circuitry mask), and no unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps are reported. Therefore the study reports ROI-restricted results (E3) and group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect (E5), violating the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain group-level maps (I6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) during scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (pump decisions) and reward (cash-outs) and uses parametric modulators and trial-based contrasts tied to risky decision-making (meets I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (age as continuous regressor) with correction for multiple comparisons and results reported in tables and figures (meets I6 and I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, GLM, PPI), Results (behavioral, fMRI activation, PPI, mediation), and Discussion; thus full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (E3), not only connectivity/resting-state (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and this is empirical fMRI work (not E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=19 included in fMRI analysis) in which participants performed a risky decision-making task (rating risk of continuing physical activities). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risky decision making (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; high-harm > low-harm; format contrasts and interactions). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM results with cluster correction and tables/figures reporting activated regions and peak coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4 (task fMRI of risky decisions), I5 (relevant contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded. Exclusion IDs met: E3, E4. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) — the fMRI paradigm is an emotional go/no-go impulse-control task, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as required; I5 (within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) — the paper does not report task contrasts such as risky>safe or high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty; I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) — analyses are ROI-based pseudo-resting-state connectivity and predictive modeling, not whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. The paper focuses on task-residual connectivity (pseudo-RS) and ROI-based PLSR prediction of "brain age" and correlations with self-report risk measures, so it meets the exclusions for ROI-only/connectivity-only reporting and lack of task-evoked whole-brain maps. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task that explicitly manipulated probabilistic (intended vs. unintended) outcomes and magnitudes, i.e., uncertainty/risk. The task and analyses include contrasts directly relevant to risky/ambiguous decision-making (e.g., unintended > intended outcomes, high- vs low-magnitude outcomes, loss vs gain) and report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical analyses (AFNI 3dttest++, cluster correction) with coordinates/tables. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete for screening. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task type (I4), relevant contrasts (I5), whole-brain group-level voxelwise evidence (I6), and acceptable reporting format (I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a two-choice color discrimination speeded reaction-time task (perceptual decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (task blocks vs no-task control; good vs bad clock; accessory vs no accessory) that index perceptual/task difficulty and expectancy, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 analyses with results presented in tables and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI perceptual decision-making (I4), contains relevant within-task contrasts (I5), provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps (I6), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I7). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (N=25) performing a two-option risky decision-making task (Selection task).
