The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to risk and valence (e.g., riskier > surer, gains > losses, parametric analyses of ∑Var, ΔVar, chosen vs unchosen EV/SV). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain GLMs with cluster-level family-wise error correction and reported peak coordinates and supplementary tables (Tables S2–S4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition, GLM), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI with a visuomotor finger-tapping task that included voluntary action selection, but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. No contrasts are reported that correspond to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguity > non-ambiguity”, or “hard > easy”). The study does report group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and clearly describes whole-brain analyses. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I4 and I5 are not satisfied; I6 and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (coherent motion direction detection). It reports a clear task contrast (Motion > Static) tied to perceptual processing and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample random-effects t test, FWE-corrected clusters) to identify V5/MT and to extract percent signal change; results are reported as activation clusters. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of task, contrasts, and whole-brain analyses. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast Motion > Static related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (results reported as activation clusters/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only without task effects, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=30) in healthy humans using a perceptual decision-making task (bistable/interhemispheric motion) performed during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., incoherent > coherent, ambiguous > static, switch-related > state), satisfying I5. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain RFX-GLM statistical maps with voxelwise correction and cluster thresholds (reported in figures/tables), satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions), so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the perceptual decision-making arm of the meta-analysis and should be included.

This study is a pharmacological fMRI investigation of reversal learning and reward feedback (positive vs. negative), not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. While the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps (meeting I6/I7) and conducts contrasts of positive vs negative feedback and switching-related contrasts, it does not report contrasts framed as risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or hard vs easy perceptual decisions. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (task domain) and I5 (relevant risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study acquired fMRI while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (texture discrimination), conducted voxelwise GLM analyses and group-level whole-brain contrasts with cluster correction, and reported task-evoked activations (task > baseline; trained vs untrained; pre vs post). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results presented in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections, so appears complete for screening purposes.

This study acquired task-based fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with monetary gains and loss-avoidance (a decision-making task with probabilistic/risky outcomes). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to experienced and expected value (e.g., [Gain – Loss-avoidance], [Positive – Neutral expected value]) and correlations with behavior/symptoms. Crucially, the authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (whole-brain t-tests and multivariate models) with tables/figures of results. Thus it satisfies I4 (task fMRI during a risky/probabilistic decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts relevant to decision outcomes), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-level whole-brain effects, empirical fMRI data provided).

Only the abstract/full-text excerpt is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract it is clear the study used fMRI while participants categorized prosodic expressions, so I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making categorization task) appears satisfied. However, the available content does not provide the full methods/results needed to verify inclusion criteria I5 (explicit within-task or between-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making, e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous or hard > easy) nor I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and crucial criteria (I5 and I6) cannot be confirmed from the provided excerpt, the study must be excluded at this stage.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly tests ambiguous decision-making: subjects performed social (approach/avoid) judgments of neutral (ambiguous) faces and a nonsocial sex-discrimination control. The main imaging contrasts compare social judgment versus sex discrimination for neutral faces (i.e., ambiguous task > control), and an ANOVA and post hoc contrasts report greater right amygdala activity for social judgment of neutral faces. Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM models with reported coordinates/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject contrasts, is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in humans that included an explicit perceptual decision-making task (odour detection: participants indicated presence/absence of odour during pre- and post-conditioning scans). The imaging analyses include within-task condition comparisons implemented as multivariate (searchlight) classification analyses (e.g., category, identity, value cross-decoding) and group-level voxelwise statistical maps (normalized/smoothed accuracy maps submitted to group-level paired t-tests and reported with peak coordinates). Results are reported at the group level with voxelwise inference (small-volume correction) and coordinates. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for (I4) an fMRI perceptual decision-making task, (I5) within-task contrasts/classification between conditions, (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps, and (I7) reporting of results with coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked maps and empirical data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is a complete empirical fMRI study using a probabilistic reversal learning task and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps (meets I6 and I7). However, the task and reported contrasts probe cognitive flexibility/reversal learning (final reversal errors v. perseverative errors, perseverative v. probabilistic errors, correct v. incorrect) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). Therefore it does not meet I4 (task type: risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) nor I5 (at least one contrast explicitly related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Decision: EXCLUDED. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: none (E: []).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making task (the Cups task). It includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Risky > Safe; Win > Loss) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and MNI coordinates. Results are presented as figures/tables of coordinates and described in text. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods (subjects, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a commentary/summary (Konovalov & Krajbich) discussing Juechems et al. (2017) rather than reporting original empirical fMRI data. The manuscript does not present methods, participants, or group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from an fMRI experiment. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). It does not satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (conducted fMRI on human participants during a task), I5 (reports within-task/between-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), or I7 (whole-brain results described). Full text appears complete (main text present).

This is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study reporting group-level voxelwise task activation maps (satisfies I6) and presents whole-brain results/tables (satisfies I7). However, the tasks and contrasts do not match the meta-analysis targets for risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I4/I5). The main task is a probabilistic reversal-learning task and a planning (Tower of London) task; reported contrasts are monetary gain vs baseline, monetary loss vs baseline, and reversal vs baseline rather than contrasts explicitly indexing risk (e.g., risky>safe), ambiguity (e.g., ambiguous>non-ambiguous), or perceptual difficulty (e.g., hard>easy). Although PRLT involves probabilistic feedback, the paper does not report within-task contrasts that clearly map onto risky or ambiguous decision-making contrasts required by the review. Therefore I4 and I5 are not met and the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Jackpot task with play vs pass choices and explicit risk levels), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts. The paper includes relevant within-task and between-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., Play vs Pass analyses and Social > Monetary Play; Social > Monetary Gain), and whole-brain group results (cluster-level FWE-corrected findings) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (only ROI/ connectivity/ non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a memory-based decision task in ambiguous (morphed) environments, matching the review’s focus on ambiguous decision-making. The authors present within-task contrasts/predictions testing sigmoidal (ambiguous) versus linear models of response and relate behavioral ambiguity to voxelwise fMRI pattern similarity, reporting group-level peak coordinates and bootstrap-corrected statistics (hippocampus and visual cortex). Whole-brain voxelwise results are implied by reporting of peak coordinates and statements about effects outside visual cortex. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is included for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making) conducted in humans during scanning, reporting a risky > safe contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (SPM8), provides coordinates and cluster-corrected results, and describes one-sample and two-sample t-tests as well as voxel-wise correlations. Results are reported as whole-brain activations (coordinates) meeting the meta-analysis reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening purposes.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing decision-making under risk (probability discounting and loss-aversion tasks) (I4). It presents within-task contrasts relating neural activity to subjective value/potential gain and loss (e.g., BOLD covariation with subjective probabilistic loss, sgACC response to potential gain, amygdala response to potential loss) and group comparisons (e.g., one-way ANOVA across suicide attempters, nonsuicidal depressed patients, and controls) (I5). The authors ran second-level/random-effects group analyses and report whole-brain exploratory analyses (uncorrected p<0.001) with activations listed in supplementary tables, alongside ROI/SVC results; thus group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported (I6, I7). The study is empirical, not ROI-only, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI)-restricted task analyses and does not provide unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group maps required by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E5 (results focused on between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria summary: no inclusion criteria are fully satisfied. Specifically, I4 is not clearly met (task is probabilistic reversal learning, which is not framed as a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast in the terms required by the review), I5 is not met (reported contrasts are reward/punishment/reversal vs baseline rather than standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts), and I6 is not met (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps are presented). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical within-subject pharmacological fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a gambling task that manipulates risk level. It reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM5) with voxelwise statistics and FWE correction, tests contrasts related to risk (e.g., aversive outcomes following low-, medium-, high-risk choices; linear risk effects), and reports stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/low-risk vs high-risk and outcome contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (coordinates and results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Recommended for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps while human participants performed a perceptual judgment task (viewing video clips and making trial-wise judgements: e.g., ‘Did you see a magic trick?’ or an attentional colour-detection task). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (Magic > Causal Control; Surprise > Causal Control; Magic > Surprise) and provides voxelwise, group-level analyses and coordinate results. Thus I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to the perceptual judgment; e.g., experimental task > control), and I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses) are satisfied. The paper also reports coordinate-level results and tables/transformations (satisfying I7). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Hence the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as a perceptual decision-making study.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (mirror vs normal word reading with a lexical decision: real word vs non-word). It includes relevant within-task contrasts (mirror > normal) that map onto perceptual difficulty comparisons (hard > easy). Data were analyzed with group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise SPM99 random-effects analyses and results reported as activation clusters and coordinates. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, and is empirical). Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between a sure amount and lotteries) with trial-by-trial parametric modulation of risk dimensions. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., gamble > sure/choice-related activity; parametric contrasts for variance and skewness) and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster- and voxel-wise FWE correction and stereotactic coordinates reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, behavioural modelling, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, GLM), Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Thus all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain task analyses of reinforcement learning (RPE) during a probabilistic social reinforcement learning task, but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Inclusion: I6 (group-level whole-brain task map reported) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described) are satisfied. Not met: I4 (task must be risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and I5 (at least one contrast related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Decision: EXCLUDED because key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that manipulated outcome probability and magnitude during a decision-related task (probabilistic monetary incentive delay). It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk/probability (e.g., 80% vs 20% PRB, linear EV, VAL×MAG, VAL×PRB) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Z maps, Talairach coordinates, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I4 is not met: during fMRI acquisition participants performed a non-phonetic alertness task (detect quieter catch trials) and did not perform an explicit perceptual decision-making task in the scanner. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study includes within-task contrasts separating /ba/ vs /da/ categories used in analyses), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise searchlight random-effects maps are reported), and I7 (whole-brain results are clearly reported in figures and text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This study used fMRI but the task is explicit moral decision-making (controversial vs. non-controversial moral phrases), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (task domain) and I5 (contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). The full text does include group-level whole-brain analyses (I6) and reports results in tables/coordinates and text (I7), but those alone do not meet the review objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dynamically adaptive motion prediction), with within-task contrasts (errors vs correct; informative vs noninformative feedback) that index perceptual/decision difficulty and uncertainty. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (z-maps, voxelwise one-sample t tests, tables of coordinates and figures). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used BOLD fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task), provided within-task parametric contrasts across risk levels, and reported group-level whole-brain activation patterns associated with risk level (described in text and figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (GLM with 9 risk-level contrasts), Results (whole-brain activations) and Discussion. Thus it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. While the study includes group-level whole-brain fMRI task activation analyses (satisfying I6) and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I7), it does NOT meet key review inclusion criteria: the fMRI scan was not performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (I4 not met). The delay-discounting (risky/impulsive choice) task was administered outside the scanner, so there is no within-scan contrast of decision-making (I5 not met). The reported fMRI contrasts (e.g., CS+ > CS−) reflect conditioned cue/reactivity (attention/reward) rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making: adolescents performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) during fMRI (meets I4). The authors modeled within-task conditions (pump decisions, cash-outs, explosions) and report task-evoked contrasts (risk decisions/pumps) used in univariate analyses and extracted parameter estimates (meets I5). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported and described (maps/tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (meets I6 and I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: the paper contains whole-brain activation results (not ROI-only), and is empirical. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), with task-versus-rest and between-group (FH+ vs FH-) voxelwise group analyses. Whole-brain, group-level statistical maps were generated using FSL/FLAME and results are reported in figures and tables of activated regions/coordinates. Although the primary contrast is task>rest rather than an explicit risky>safe contrast, it constitutes an experimental task (risk) > control comparison that maps task-evoked risk-related activation. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion so is complete for screening.

This study used an n-back working memory task (0-back vs 2-back), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Therefore it does not meet I4 (task domain) nor I5 (task-related contrast for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrast reported) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E5) apply. Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5. Exclusion IDs met: none ([]).

Exclusion E3 met: activation analyses were constrained to an a priori mask (reward-learning regions), i.e. effectively ROI-restricted, and no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the decision-making contrasts is reported. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is a reward-learning monetary RPE task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review), I5 (contrasts are RPE/RE/OE, not risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy perceptual contrasts), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported; activation was ROI-masked). Full text appears complete. Therefore study is not eligible for this meta-analysis of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants (N=23) that implemented a perceptual decision-making task with covertly interspersed ambiguous trials and explicit behavioral reports. The experiment acquired task-evoked BOLD (3T, whole-brain EPI) and performed group-level, voxelwise GLMs with parametric modulators and reported whole-brain results (FWE-corrected and uncorrected thresholds) and coordinate tables; ROI and whole-brain contrasts relate directly to perceptual decision processes (e.g., ambiguous vs. unambiguous effects reflected in model-based regressors, ‘tilt > baseline’, and regressors for low-level vs. high-level predictions). Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (task-related contrasts relevant to perceptual-DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in text/tables). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making task (choices between a certain monetary amount and a gamble). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., gamble vs certain choices; analyses of risky vs non-risky choices and value-related contrasts). Group-level voxelwise GLMs and second-level one-sample t-tests were conducted and coordinate-level results (MNI coordinates, Z values) are reported; whole-brain analyses were performed (with ROI-based SVC for hypothesis testing). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy humans performing a perceptual sequence task requiring detection of order deviants (perceptual decision-making), meeting I4. It reports within-task contrasts comparing anticipation conditions (high vs. low prior probability), satisfying I5. The authors ran group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported in the whole-brain analysis section, albeit showing no FWE-corrected significant clusters), meeting I6, and this null whole-brain result is described in the text, satisfying I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting) apply, as a whole-brain analysis was performed and reported (even if null). Note: although primary positive results are from ROI analyses, the presence of a reported group-level whole-brain analysis supports inclusion for a meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies. Confidence moderate due to reliance on reported null whole-brain findings rather than positive whole-brain peaks.

This is an fMRI study that implemented a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) during whole-brain scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., risky vs safe, group-by-decision interactions), uses voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster correction (AlphaSim) and reports coordinates/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (risk-related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face same/different discrimination with morph continua). It includes within-task contrasts tied to perceptual difficulty/objective similarity (subjective ‘same’ vs ‘different’ and parametric modulation by morphing distance; triple/quadruple interactions testing Test and Group), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with second-level random-effects and correction procedures; results are presented in text/tables/figures. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supplementary descriptions).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that used a perceptual/ambiguous decision-making task (subjects judged ambiguous auditory stimuli as word vs pseudoword) during scanning, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing word- versus pseudoword-perceived trials and phase-specific activations with corrected thresholds and coordinates. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous/perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task contrast related to ambiguity: word-perceived vs pseudoword-perceived), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study should be excluded because the MRI data are resting-state connectivity analyses and not task-evoked fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI conducted while performing a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), and I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). No inclusion criteria are satisfied. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the decision-making task inclusion criteria. Specifically, the fMRI task is a passive cue-viewing task (cocaine-related vs. natural scene pictures) and is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (I4 not met). Consequently, there are no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I5 not met). The study does report group-level whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps (I6 met) and reports results in figures/coordinates/text (I7 met). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults using a gambling/guessing task that manipulates reward probability and magnitude (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., gain > loss; probability and magnitude effects; EV+ and EV− contrasts) and uses group-level, random-effects, voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain results and corrected statistics, with coordinates and figures. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I6) and reports whole-brain results in figures/tables (meets I7). However, during fMRI scanning participants passively viewed Igo stimuli and were instructed not to solve problems, so no risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task was performed in-scanner (I4 not met). The reported contrasts (Igo vs non-Igo, Day3 vs Day1, learning-related changes) reflect learning-related responsivity differences rather than within-task contrasts that index perceptual decision-making difficulty or uncertainty (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence), so I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I4 and I5.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a gambling/slot-machine task (risky decision-making), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results and contrasts reported. Relevant within-task contrasts include wins vs all non-wins and near-misses vs full-misses, and an interaction (near-miss × personal choice). Whole-brain results are reported with voxelwise FWE-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables. The article therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts relevant to decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I7 (results presented as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that implements probabilistic discounting (PD; a risky decision-making task) and delayed discounting during task fMRI. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts of subjective value for PD and DD, presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results (coordinates and statistical maps reported; SVC was applied but analyses were conducted at the whole-brain second level), and provides coordinate tables and figures. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/probability), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity/no whole-brain results, non-empirical paper, or only between-group without task effect) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials not required. Therefore include for meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in human PD patients performing a probabilistic ‘roulette’ reward task that manipulates stake and winning probability (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task task-evoked contrasts (outcome-induced activations and trial-by-trial regressions with reward prediction error derived from stake×probability) and categorical analyses of negative vs positive RPEs, which relate directly to risk/uncertainty processing. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses are reported with corrected coordinates and tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI with whole-brain group analyses (I6) and reported whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I7). However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. The task is a monetary incentive delay paradigm probing reward anticipation and outcome (reward vs neutral), without manipulations of risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty and without contrasts such as "risky > safe", "ambiguity > non-ambiguous", or "hard > easy". Therefore it fails to meet I4 (task domain) and I5 (relevant contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (reporting perceived motion direction) and includes classification of ambiguous vs unambiguous percepts. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a perceptual decision task) and I5 (within-task contrast predicting reported percept: 45° vs 135°). However, the paper reports ROI-based MVPA and ROI statistics rather than a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. No unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or group-level whole-brain contrasts are reported, so it violates E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet I6. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain BOLD data while healthy participants performed a forced-choice valence categorization of faces (a perceptual/ambiguous decision-making task). The reported within-task contrasts examine incongruent > congruent conditions (separately by emotion), directly indexing interference/ambiguity effects in decision-making. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (SPM2) with tables of coordinates, conjunction and interaction analyses, and ROI percent-signal-change results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, trial design, image acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and imaging), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; not between-group-only; empirical study with original fMRI data). Therefore the study satisfies I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

While this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study reporting voxelwise group-level contrasts (I6, I7) and includes within-task contrasts comparing high vs low reward probability (I5), it does not meet I4: participants did not perform a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task in the sense required by the meta-analysis. The task involved passive observation of probability cues and an expectedness judgment, not choices under risk/ambiguity or perceptual discrimination decisions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore, exclude because inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied.

This study used fMRI to assess cue-reactivity (smoking-related vs neutral stimuli) and a Go/No-Go response-inhibition task, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. No contrasts relate to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Neuroimaging analyses were restricted to predefined ROI masks (voxelwise tests within an ROI mask) rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses) and does not meet inclusion criteria I4–I7. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task type), I5 (relevant contrasts), I6 (whole-brain task map), I7 (reporting acceptable for whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a card-gambling task that manipulates risk and monetary reward. It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk wins > low-risk wins, risk-choice linear contrast), presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (with FWE-corrected clusters and tables/figures), and provides sufficient methods, results, and discussion in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) and supplementary material is not required for eligibility.

This fMRI study examined visual food-cue perception (Food > Non-Food) in genotype groups; it is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (no perceptual decision difficulty contrasts like hard>easy or coherence manipulations). Key inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is food-cue reactivity/visual perception rather than a perceptual decision-making paradigm), I5 (no within-task contrast that indexes risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making; contrasts are Food > Non-Food and tastiness parametric effects, not decision-difficulty or uncertainty contrasts), and I6 (the reported target analyses were constrained to the posterior fusiform gyrus with small-volume correction rather than a reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the decision-related contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) strictly apply based on the full text (whole-brain results are referenced in Supplementary Material but not as decision-making contrasts). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s required inclusion criteria for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that includes a perceptual decision-making task (Color task: detect dot color changes) and reports task-related contrasts (e.g., Intention vs Color and Color vs Intention, as well as condition contrasts). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses with cluster correction and coordinates/tables of activations reported. Thus the study satisfies I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision task), I5 (between-task/perceptual task contrasts reported), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group without task effect, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
